sources.role: the decision that the live animals and high-risk plants party pickers page at eight, and that the one-page clause of inc-087's criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped along with req-594, req-595 and the paging and inset half of c-094's outcome. The clause rested on ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-041, which that file heads as the orchestrator's application of Sam's principle rather than a ruling of Sam's: point 3b is about live filtering alone, and the bullet three lines above builds the INS address book list at 8 a page over the same records. The prototype's single page is read off a book too small to need paging, so it is evidence either way only under ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116, which keeps the prototype to look and feel rather than architecture; ruling:ian-2026-11-11 point 2 is not the ground, being scoped to app/data and data claims. Eight is the INS address book list's figure alone: the transporter list renders no pagination yet, EUDPA-824 being To Do. The 'Selected address' inset comes back with the paging, because req-595's own reason for dropping it was that one page put the chosen row always on screen. req-611 is unaffected: the address book's role-scoped list stays unpaginated, because each frontend reads the whole book to filter by role and pages what is left for display.

claims.statement: The live animals and high-risk plants party pickers show eight of a role's addresses a page.
claims.quote: The pickers page at eight, and the one-page clause of `inc-087`'s criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped.
claims.note: New. Answers the report question the bug raised against inc-087 criterion 7.

claims.statement: The one-page clause of inc-087's acceptance criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped.
claims.quote: the one-page clause of `inc-087`'s criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped
claims.note: New. The clause this ruling withdraws, named by criterion.

claims.statement: Eight a page is the figure the INS address book list already uses, which is why the pickers take it.
claims.quote: Eight is the figure the INS address book list already uses (`insfrontend:src/server/app/features/address-book/list/list.controller.js:49`, `REQ-INS-ADDR-013`).
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The animals transporter list is not a precedent for how many addresses a page holds, because it renders no pagination today and the ticket to split it into pages of eight is still to do.
claims.quote: The animals transporter list is **not** a precedent: it renders no pagination today, and EUDPA-824, the ticket to split it into pages of eight, is still To Do.
claims.note: New. Refuses a precedent rather than setting one.

claims.statement: Paging the pickers sits on top of the role filtering, which stays as it is.
claims.quote: Paging comes back on top of the role filtering, which is correct and stays.
claims.note: New. Leaves the role filtering inc-087 built untouched.

claims.statement: The one-page clause was a distillation error: it rests on a claim that is the orchestrator's application of Sam's principle on live filtering, not a ruling of Sam's on how many addresses a page holds.
claims.quote: **It was a distillation error, and the error is identifiable.** The clause rests on `ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-041`, which is the orchestrator's application of Sam's principle, not a ruling of Sam's on paging
claims.note: New. Names the claim the withdrawn clause rested on.

claims.statement: Sam's point 3b rules on when results refresh, not on how many addresses a page holds.
claims.quote: It rules on when results refresh, not on how many a page holds.
claims.note: New. The ground on which the earlier claim is read as not covering paging.

claims.statement: The same afternoon ruling builds the INS address book list at eight a page three lines above the sentence that removed the pickers' paging, over the same address-book records, so one page of it holds two incompatible answers, and eight is the one with a requirement behind it.
claims.quote: One ruling, one page of it, two incompatible answers to how many addresses a page holds. Eight is the one with a requirement behind it.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The prototype showing one page of addresses is a fixture of an address book too small to need paging, not a requirement that a page holds every address.
claims.quote: **The prototype's single page is a fixture, not a requirement.** `prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-063` reads one page off the prototype's own address book, which holds too few records to need paging, so the prototype could not show paging whether it wanted it or not.
claims.note: New. Sets aside the prototype claim behind the one-page clause.

claims.statement: How many rows a page holds over a real dataset that grows is not look and feel, so the prototype is not the authority for it.
claims.quote: It rests instead on `ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116`, "Prototype is the authority for how things look and feel not how they are architected": how many rows a page holds over a real dataset that grows is not look and feel

claims.statement: The "Selected address: <name>" restatement comes back with the paging, between the search box and the results, in the words both frontends already had.
claims.quote: The inset goes back where it was, between the search box and the results, with the words both frontends already had.
claims.note: New. Reverses req-595's removal of the inset.

claims.statement: The reason req-595 gave for dropping the restatement no longer holds, because the chosen row can be on another page again and a trader on page two would otherwise have nothing on screen telling them what they have chosen.
claims.quote: Once the chosen row can be on another page again, that reason is gone: a trader on page two would otherwise have nothing on screen telling them what they have chosen.

claims.statement: The address book's own role-scoped list stays unpaginated: each frontend reads the whole book because the list endpoint takes no role, filters by role itself, and then pages what is left for display.
claims.quote: The address book's own role-scoped list stays unpaginated: each frontend reads the whole book because the list endpoint takes no role, filters by role itself, and then pages what is left for display. Paging the API would make the role filter wrong.

claims.statement: inc-087 stays done, because it was built as its criteria then read, and the code, the criteria, the requirements behind them, c-094's outcome and the behaviour spec are corrected under EUDPA-827 so a re-distillation does not drop paging or the restatement again.

sources.role: the decision that the exporter clause of inc-087 acceptance criterion 2 is dropped and no EXPORTER role is to be added anywhere. The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

sources.role: what exists today and what has already been ruled; the real persistence, validation and cross-service constraints the prototype cannot express

claims.statement: A notification is stored as one document in the MongoDB collection named "notification".
claims.quote: @org.springframework.data.mongodb.core.mapping.Document(collection = "notification")

claims.statement: The stored notification holds its identity and metadata at the top level and its content (parties, commodity, transport and so on) as a nested notification sub-object, beside a separate fulfilments payload.
claims.quote: Aggregate root: identity + metadata at the top, with the well-structured content held as a composed {@link Notification} sub-object (symmetric with the opaque {@link #fulfilments} payload).

claims.statement: Each stored notification has a string id as its database identity.
claims.quote:
@Id
    private String id;

claims.statement: A notification's reference number is unique across all notifications, and the unique index is sparse, so notifications without a reference number are allowed and do not clash with each other.
claims.quote:
@Indexed(unique = true, sparse = true)
    private String referenceNumber;

claims.statement: Each notification carries a concurrencyToken that is the record's optimistic-locking version number.
claims.quote:
@Version
    private Long concurrencyToken;

claims.statement: Each notification carries a status, one of the NotificationStatus values.
claims.quote: private NotificationStatus status;

claims.statement: Each notification records when it was created and when it was last updated, as instants (moments in time), stamped by the server.
claims.quote:
private Instant created;

    private Instant updated;

claims.statement: A client cannot set a notification's created or updated time: the request shape has no such fields and the server would discard them.
claims.quote: the aggregate's server-stamped {@code created}/{@code updated} instants are deliberately absent here; a client cannot set them and the server would discard them.

claims.statement: Each notification records submittedAt, the time of its most recent submission: set the first time it is submitted from DRAFT and refreshed whenever it is re-submitted from AMEND.
claims.quote: Timestamp of the most recent submission — set the first time the notification is submitted (from DRAFT) and refreshed whenever it is re-submitted from AMEND.

claims.statement: Starting an amendment or cancelling one leaves submittedAt unchanged, so it always points at the latest submission rather than the original one.
claims.quote: Left unchanged by amend and cancel-amend, so it always points at the latest submission event rather than the original one. Set by {@code submitNotification}; carried into the fulfilment-view projection.

claims.statement: A notification created through the app in a non-production environment carries an expiry time (expireAt), anchored to its created time, after which it becomes eligible for automatic expiry.
claims.quote: When this notification becomes eligible for automatic expiry, anchored to {@code created}. Set only for app-created notifications in non-prod environments

claims.statement: In production, and for notifications created before the expiry field existed, a notification has no expiry time.
claims.quote: {@code null} in prod and for notifications created before this field existed.

claims.statement: Expiry is driven by a sweep over a plain index rather than a database TTL index, so expiring a notification can also remove its accompanying documents.
claims.quote: Backed by a plain index (not a Mongo TTL index) so the expiry sweep can cascade to accompanying documents.

claims.statement: The expiry time is never shown in any JSON response.
Each notification stores a fulfilments payload (a list of documents recording obligation fulfilment) exactly as sent, byte for byte; the backend never interprets it.
claims.quote: Opaque obligation-fulfilment payload — persisted byte-faithfully; never interpreted by the backend.

claims.statement: When an amendment starts, the notification's content is snapshotted as it stood (including inline party details); cancelling the amendment restores that snapshot, and submitting the amendment clears it.
claims.quote: Pre-amend snapshot of {@link #notification}. Amend-only scratchpad: captured when an amendment starts, restored by cancel-amend, and cleared when the amendment is submitted. Independent of {@link #preAmendFulfilments}; carries inline party details as they stood when the trader opened the amendment.

claims.statement: The fulfilments payload is snapshotted separately when an amendment starts, restored by cancelling the amendment and cleared when it is submitted, independently of the content snapshot.
claims.quote: Pre-amend snapshot of {@link #fulfilments}. Amend-only scratchpad: restored by cancel-amend and cleared when the amendment is submitted. Independent of the content freeze.

claims.statement: Neither pre-amendment snapshot is ever shown in a JSON response.
claims.quote:
@JsonIgnore
    private Notification preAmendNotification;

claims.statement: Wherever the backend needs a notification's content, a record with no content sub-object fails at once with an error rather than carrying on; the unexpected-error handler would turn that into a 500 response.
claims.quote:
return requireNonNull(notification,
            "NotificationAggregate requires a notification sub-object at this seam");
claims.note: Inferred that the failure reaches a caller as 500: a NullPointerException is a RuntimeException, which GlobalExceptionHandler.handleException maps to 500. Which endpoints reach this seam is parts 2 and 3.

claims.statement: A request to save a notification has a body with a notification object, which is required, and an optional actor object.
A save request without a notification object is rejected with a 400 validation error naming the notification field.
claims.quote:
@NotNull
    NotificationDto notification;
claims.note: Inferred from @NotNull together with the MethodArgumentNotValidException handler. NotificationController applies @Valid to the SaveNotificationDto body at lines 52 (POST /notifications) and 71 (PUT by reference number); which endpoints those are is parts 2 and 3. The message would be the Bean Validation default ("must not be null").

claims.statement: The actor on a save request identifies who made the change: an id, a source, a user type, a display name, an organisation id and the organisation id acted on behalf of; it is passed on as the actor of the change.
claims.note: ActorRequest is not in this part's read list; it was read because SaveNotificationDto names it. Where the actor goes (the outbox Actor) is part 5.

claims.statement: The notification object in a request carries the content fields plus referenceNumber, status, concurrencyToken and the fulfilments payload.
The request shape is only ever inbound: no endpoint returns it; every endpoint returns the stored notification or one of its view projections.
claims.quote: It is never a response body — every endpoint returns {@link NotificationAggregate} or one of the view projections

claims.statement: The request shape is also the internal carrier the copy feature uses to create a new notification from an existing one.
claims.quote: Inbound request shape: the {@code notification} member of {@link SaveNotificationDto}, and the internal carrier {@link NotificationCopyMapper} hands to the create path.

claims.statement: No content field of the notification carries a validation constraint: the backend accepts any section or field missing or empty, with no required fields, lengths or formats enforced on the content.
claims.ref: src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/animals/notification/NotificationBase.java:12-50 and the section types Origin, Commodity, CommodityComplement, Species, AnimalIdentifier, Transport, Transporter, Address, ConsignmentParty, AdditionalDetails
claims.note: Inferred from absence: grep for jakarta.validation.constraints across src/main/java finds it only in SaveNotificationDto, NotificationController, DocumentUploadRequest and configuration classes; no domain type in notification/ has a constraint, so the cascading @Valid on notification has nothing to check.

claims.statement: The backend records no rule for which fields a notification must have before it can be submitted, nor any length or format rule for free-text fields such as the CPH number, email, phone or postcode.
claims.ref: src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/animals/notification/ (every domain type read in this part)
claims.note: Looked in every domain type in this slice and in GlobalExceptionHandler. Whether submit checks completeness in the service is part 2's to say.

claims.statement: The same content fields are shared by the stored content sub-object and the request shape.
claims.quote: Shared content fields extended by {@link Notification} (content sub-object) and {@link NotificationDto} (wire type).

claims.statement: A date-only field sent as a date-time, such as 2026-07-21T00:00:00Z or 2026-07-21T00:00:00, is rejected with a 400 rather than having its time part silently dropped.

A caller that sends a moment where a calendar date belongs would then be told 200, and the day it meant would depend on a zone nobody stated. With leniency off the value fails to parse and the caller gets 400.

A poller publishes waiting outbox events on a fixed delay of outbox.poller.interval-ms, 2000 ms by default.
claims.quote: @Scheduled(fixedDelayString = "${outbox.poller.interval-ms:2000}")

claims.statement: The poller is on unless outbox.poller.enabled is set to false.
claims.quote: @ConditionalOnProperty(prefix = "outbox.poller", name = "enabled", havingValue = "true", matchIfMissing = true)

claims.statement: Only one backend instance publishes at a time: each poll takes a shared lock named outbox-poller, held for at least 1 second and at most 30 seconds.
claims.quote: static final String LOCK_NAME = "outbox-poller";

claims.statement: The poller reads waiting events 10 at a time and publishes at most 500 in one run; the run limit can be set with OUTBOX_POLLER_MAX_EVENTS_PER_RUN.
claims.quote:
batch-size: 10
    max-events-per-run: ${OUTBOX_POLLER_MAX_EVENTS_PER_RUN:500}

claims.statement: A batch size or run limit of zero or less falls back to 10 and 500, and lock times left unset fall back to 1 and 30 seconds; the poll interval must be positive or the service will not start.
Events are published to one SNS topic, set by OUTBOX_SNS_TOPIC_ARN; when no topic is set, the poller publishes nothing and events stay waiting.
claims.note: OutboxConfig marks topicArn @NotBlank while application.yml defaults it to empty, so a missing value may instead stop the service from starting. The publish code is written to tolerate it.

claims.statement: The topic is an SNS FIFO topic: each message's group id is the notification's aggregateId and its deduplication id is the eventId.

.messageGroupId(event.getAggregateId())

Once an event is published it is marked with its publish time and is never published again by the poller.
A run keeps reading batches until no events are waiting, a publish fails, or the run limit is reached.

claims.statement: The service serves the list of countries at GET /countries.
claims.quote: @RequestMapping("/countries")

claims.statement: GET /countries takes one optional query parameter, blocks.
claims.quote: @RequestParam(required = false, value = "blocks") String blocks

claims.statement: GET /countries returns 200 with a JSON array of countries.
claims.quote: return ResponseEntity.ok(countries);

claims.statement: GET /countries returns countries sorted by their name.
claims.quote: .sorted(Comparator.comparing(Country::getName))

claims.statement: The country sort is a plain case-sensitive string comparison of the name, not a locale-aware collation, so names are ordered by character code.
claims.quote: Comparator.comparing(Country::getName)
claims.note: Comparator.comparing on a String uses String.compareTo; no Collator is applied.

claims.statement: The United Kingdom (effectiveAlpha2 GB) is always removed from the countries list, whatever blocks value is asked for.
claims.quote: .filter(c -> !"GB".equals(c.getEffectiveAlpha2()))

claims.statement: When blocks is given, a country is kept only if one of its MDM blocks has a name equal to the blocks value and includeCountry true.
When blocks is not given, no block filter is applied and every country except the United Kingdom is returned.
claims.quote: if (requestedBlock == null || country.getBlocks() == null) return true;

claims.statement: When blocks is given but MDM sends a country with no blocks list at all, that country is kept rather than filtered out.
claims.quote: if (requestedBlock == null || country.getBlocks() == null) return true;

claims.statement: The blocks value is also passed to MDM as its own blocks query parameter, so MDM filters first and the service filters again on includeCountry.
claims.quote: mdmClient.getCountries(ocpApimSubscriptionKey, SYSTEM, blocks);

claims.statement: The block filter compares the whole blocks value with a single block name, so asking for several blocks at once in one value (for example comma-separated) would match no country unless MDM names a block that way.
claims.quote: requestedBlock.equals(b.getName())
claims.note: No splitting of the blocks value is done anywhere in the service.

claims.statement: The block names used in tests are GBNAG_SPS_EX, GBNAG_PHYTO_EX and OMR; the service has no fixed list of allowed block values and accepts any string.
claims.quote: restTemplate.getForEntity("/countries?blocks=GBNAG_PHYTO_EX", String.class);
claims.note: No validation of the blocks parameter exists in the controller or service.

claims.statement: Each returned country has a code field, taken from MDM's effectiveAlpha2 (the ISO alpha-2 code).
claims.quote: this.code = mdmCountry.getEffectiveAlpha2();

claims.statement: Each returned country has a name field, taken from MDM's effectiveAlias (the short display name, such as "United Kingdom"), not MDM's name or longName.
claims.quote: this.name = mdmCountry.getEffectiveAlias();

claims.statement: Each returned country has a subDivisions field: a list of its subdivisions, and an empty list when MDM sends none or a null list.
claims.quote:
if (mdmSubDivisions == null || mdmSubDivisions.isEmpty()) {
      return List.of();

claims.statement: Each subdivision has a code field taken from MDM's code.value (such as ES-CN).
claims.quote: .code(subDivision.getCode().getValue())

claims.statement: Each subdivision has a name field taken from MDM's subdivision name (such as Canary Islands).
claims.quote: .name(subDivision.getName())

claims.statement: A subdivision MDM sends with no code, or a code with no value, is dropped from the country's subdivisions.
claims.quote:
.filter(subDivision -> subDivision.getCode() != null
            && subDivision.getCode().getValue() != null)

claims.statement: Subdivisions are returned in the order MDM sends them; they are not sorted.
claims.quote: return mdmSubDivisions.stream()
claims.note: No sort is applied in mapSubDivisions or anywhere else to subdivisions.

claims.statement: A country is returned with only code, name and subDivisions: MDM's longName, name, independent, statusName, system, systemAlias, systemAlpha2, systemAlpha3, systemLongName, effectiveAlpha3, effectiveLongName and blocks are all dropped.
An MDM subdivision's blocs list is dropped; a subdivision is returned with only code and name.
claims.quote: private List<String> blocs;

A subdivision code arrives from MDM wrapped in an object with a single value field.

claims.statement: The stub simulates the DEFRA address lookup gateway's address search at GET /simulator/address-lookup/v2.1/addresses.
claims.quote: @GetMapping("/simulator/address-lookup/v2.1/addresses")

claims.statement: The simulator stands in for the address lookup gateway that the INS backend calls, as part of the EUDPA-390 address lookup spike.
claims.quote: # EUDPA-390 address lookup spike — the three federated-credential simulators (plan Step 6).
claims.note: The caller being ins-backend is stated in the application.yml comment at line 115: "The audience ins-backend's Entra token request resolves to".

claims.statement: The search accepts two optional query parameters: postcode and find (free text).
claims.quote:
@RequestParam(required = false) String postcode,
        @RequestParam(required = false) String find

claims.statement: When both postcode and find are sent, postcode is used and find is ignored.
claims.quote: String term = postcode != null ? postcode : find;

claims.statement: A postcode and a find term are matched the same way, against the same reserved terms: the simulator deliberately does not model what find really matches (a postcode, building name or number, street or town), leaving that to the real gateway in dev.
claims.quote: Deliberately identical for both parameters. What find really matches — a postcode, a building name or number, a street, a town — is a question only the real gateway can answer, and a simulator that guessed would look like an answer. Local runs prove the plumbing carries the parameter through; dev settles the behaviour.

claims.statement: When neither postcode nor find is sent, the simulator answers 400 with a JSON body whose message is "Either postcode or find is required".
claims.quote: .body("{ \"statusCode\": 400, \"message\": \"Either postcode or find is required\" }");

claims.statement: Reserved terms are matched exactly, case and spacing included, so a postcode sent in lower case or without its space (for example sw1a 1aa or SW1A1AA) does not hit a fixture and gets the no-results answer.
claims.quote:
return switch (term) {
            case "SW1A 1AA" -> jsonOk(THREE_ADDRESSES_FIXTURE);
claims.note: Inferred from the Java string switch, which compares exactly, and the default branch returning NO_RESULTS_FIXTURE. Whether callers normalise the postcode before sending it is outside this source.

claims.statement: Searching for postcode SW1A 1AA returns 200 with a JSON body holding the three fixture addresses.
claims.quote: case "SW1A 1AA" -> jsonOk(THREE_ADDRESSES_FIXTURE);

claims.statement: Searching for postcode ZZ1 1ZZ returns 204 No Content with no body: the reserved no-results postcode.
claims.quote: case "ZZ1 1ZZ" -> ResponseEntity.noContent().build();

claims.statement: Searching for postcode QQ1 1QQ returns 400 with a JSON body whose message is "Requested postcode is not valid": the reserved invalid postcode.
claims.quote: .body("{\"statusCode\":400,\"message\":\"Requested postcode is not valid\"}");

claims.statement: Searching for postcode XX1 1XX returns 503 with a JSON body whose message is "Service Unavailable": the reserved throttled or unavailable postcode.
claims.quote: .body("{\"statusCode\":503,\"message\":\"Service Unavailable\"}");

claims.statement: Searching for postcode YY1 1YY returns 200 with an HTML body ("Bad Gateway") instead of JSON: the reserved proxy-error postcode.
claims.quote: case "YY1 1YY" -> ResponseEntity.ok().contentType(MediaType.TEXT_HTML).body("<html><body>Bad Gateway</body></html>");

claims.statement: Searching for postcode TT1 1TT waits 15 seconds, then returns 200 with the three fixture addresses: the reserved slow-response postcode.
claims.quote: Thread.sleep(15_000);

claims.statement: The free-text terms "Buckingham Palace" and "Downing Street" each return 200 with the three fixture addresses, so the find search can be demonstrated locally.
claims.quote: case "Buckingham Palace", "Downing Street" -> jsonOk(THREE_ADDRESSES_FIXTURE);

claims.statement: A result for a reserved free-text term says nothing about whether the same search would return results from the real gateway: the free-text terms are fixtures, not a model of find.
claims.quote: These are reserved terms like the postcodes above, NOT a model of what find matches — that is the question the spike exists to answer, and only the real gateway can. A search here returning results says nothing about whether the same search would return results in dev.

claims.statement: Every other postcode or free-text term returns 200 with a JSON body holding no results: header totalResults "0" and an empty results list.
claims.quote: { "header": { "totalResults": "0" }, "results": [] }

claims.quote:
"header": { "totalResults": "3" },

claims.statement: The fixtures follow the real gateway's dev response of 17 September 2026, not the published v2.1 specification.
claims.quote: Shaped like the real dev response of 2026-09-17, not like the published v2.1 specification

claims.statement: The three fixture addresses are the three ways a name lands in a result (the whole name in subBuildingName; a building number and street; a sub-building, building name and street), chosen because they make composing address line 1 awkward; the Buckingham Palace case is the one dev actually returned.
claims.quote: The three results are the three ways a name lands, which is what makes composing address line 1 awkward — the first is the Buckingham Palace case dev actually returned, where {@code subBuildingName} carries the whole name and {@code buildingName}, {@code buildingNumber} and {@code street} are all null.

claims.statement: Every search requires a bearer token: the simulator checks the authorisation scheme, the token's signature, its audience and its expiry before answering any search, the way a real resource server would.
claims.quote: Checks the bearer token the way a real resource server would — signature, audience, expiry — before serving the reserved-postcode fixtures
claims.note: Described in general terms only, as the brief requires.

claims.statement: A search with a missing or invalid bearer token is refused with 401 and the JSON body { "statusCode": 401, "message": "Unauthorized. Access token is missing or invalid." }, word for word what the real gateway returned in dev on 17 September 2026.
claims.quote: .body("{ \"statusCode\": 401, \"message\": \"Unauthorized. Access token is missing or invalid.\" }");

claims.statement: The 401 answer carries no WWW-Authenticate header, matching the real gateway.
claims.quote: The gateway sends no {@code WWW-Authenticate} header with it, and neither does this.

claims.statement: The bearer check runs before the search terms are looked at, so an unauthorised request gets 401 even when it sends no search term or a reserved term.

The audience the simulator expects is set by address-lookup-simulator.expected-audience, overridable with ADDRESS_LOOKUP_SIMULATOR_EXPECTED_AUDIENCE, and must match the INS backend's local and stack Scope value exactly, api:// prefix included.
claims.quote:
# The audience ins-backend's Entra token request resolves to once /.default is stripped — must
  # match the local/stack "Scope" value in the EUDPA-390 plan exactly, api:// prefix included.
claims.note: The default value is a placeholder identifier, not a secret, and is not repeated here.

claims.statement: The simulator, like the real gateway in dev, accepts only the api:// form of the audience and refuses a token whose audience is the bare identifier.
claims.quote:
# The real gateway policy in dev wants the api:// form and rejects the bare GUID, so this does
  # too: a simulator that accepted either would not have caught the 401 the spike hit.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint requires an Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key request header; Spring rejects a request without it, so a call with no key is refused (a bad request) rather than answered.
claims.note: The header is required by default (@RequestHeader with no required=false). The 400 outcome is Spring's default for a missing required header, not code in the stub.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint takes an optional blocks query parameter but does not filter on it: every call returns the whole fixture, whichever block is asked for or if none is.

Outside this slice, trade-imports-reference-data's MdmService passes system GBNAG and blocks to MDM and then filters the answer by block itself (isIncludedInRequestedBlock), so on the stack the filtering a user sees is done by reference-data, not by the stub.

A country's block membership is a record of the block name, an includeCountry boolean and a list of string tags.
A subdivision record carries a code (an object holding a single value string), a name and a list of blocs (spelt blocs, not blocks).

claims.statement: Every request into the set enters the set's context before authentication runs, and every route is wrapped so it runs in that context.
claims.note: mechanism: carries the ambient set id through a request so set-keyed stores (dispatch index, journey flow, obligations, records, session) resolve to this set.

claims.statement: The entry guard runs before every handler in the set and, when it names a target, redirects there and stops the request.
The set refuses to mount when it has left any required seam unconfigured, naming each one.
The set refuses to mount when any of its journey cookies was not registered on the server.
Boot refuses an obligation model that carries any display key, such as a label, title or hint: display wording may not live in the obligation model.
Boot refuses the set when two pages both claim to collect the same obligation, naming the obligation and both pages.
Boot refuses the set when any obligation that is not system-populated is collected by no page, naming each uncovered obligation.
An obligation id may not contain a path metacharacter ('.', '[' or ']'), and boot refuses one that does.
claims.quote:
const ID_UNSAFE = /[.[\]]/
...
      throw new Error(
        `Obligation id "${obligation.name}" (at ${templatePath}) contains a path ` +
          `metacharacter ('.', '[' or ']') — ids must be path-safe`
      )

claims.statement: Boot also refuses the set when a feature's fulfilment bindings do not cover every obligation, and when a party binding is not scalar.
claims.quote:
assertObligationPurity()
        assertFulfilmentBindingCoverage()
        assertPartyBindingsAreScalar()
claims.note: The assertion names say what they refuse; the assertion bodies live in bridge/fulfilment-registry.js and features/addresses/assert-party-bindings.js, outside this part's slice.

claims.statement: A derived page or section gate consulted before the obligation-to-page index is built raises an error rather than silently gating every page and section out.
claims.quote:
throw new Error(
    'Derived gate consulted before the dispatch index exists — call ' +
      'buildDispatch() at boot first (an empty index would silently gate ' +
      'every page and section out)'
  )

claims.statement: The contact-address section holds one page, the consignment contact select page.
The review section holds three pages in order, the notification view, the declaration and the confirmation, and opens only when the journey is ready for check your answers.

claims.statement: A journey is ready for check your answers when every task row leaves the trader nothing to do, that is when each row reads fulfilled, not applicable or optional.
claims.quote:
/** True for a status that leaves nothing for the trader to do: fulfilled, not
 * applicable or optional. */
export const rowReady = (status) =>
  status === FULFILLED || status === NA || status === OPTIONAL

export const readyForCheckYourAnswers = (answers, inScope, evaluation) =>
  journeyTaskRows().every((row) =>
    rowReady(journeyRowStatus(row, answers, inScope, evaluation))
  )

claims.statement: The answer sections are the seven sections other than review, so a section list used for answering excludes the review.
A page with no authored gate applies when at least one obligation it collects is in scope; a page that collects nothing always applies.
An authored gate on a page replaces both the derived scope test and the required-earlier-answer test, so a page that states its own gate is never held back for a missing earlier answer.
claims.quote:
const prerequisitesAllowPage = (page, scope) =>
  Boolean(page.gate) || earliestMissingAnswerPage(page.id, scope) === undefined

export const pageGatePasses = (page, scope) =>
  prerequisitesAllowPage(page, scope) && pageAppliesTo(page, scope)

claims.statement: A section's prerequisite answers are those of its first page, so a section is held back by the same earlier answers its first page needs.
Exactly two answers are enforced at Save and continue, the country of origin and the commodity code, and they are the only answers a later page can be held back for.
claims.quote:
export const ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE = new Set([
  'countryOfOrigin',
  'commodityCode'

claims.statement: A page is held back only by those enforced answers whose own page comes earlier than it in the journey's page order, so an enforced answer asked later in the flow never blocks an earlier page.
claims.quote:
const continueOwnersBefore = (flowIndex) =>
  continueObligationOwners().filter(
    (owner) => owner.flowIndex !== -1 && owner.flowIndex < flowIndex
  )

const continuePrereqsBefore = (flowIndex) =>
  continueOwnersBefore(flowIndex).map((owner) => owner.id)

claims.statement: When a trader reaches a page whose required earlier answers are missing, they are sent to the page that asks for the earliest missing one in page order, and the page they tried to open is recorded with every missing answer id.
Save and continue goes to the next page in journey order that applies to this consignment, skipping any page that does not apply.
claims.quote:
const next = pages
    .slice(index + 1)
    .filter(isStep)
    .find((page) => pageAppliesTo(page, scope))
  if (!next) {
    return undefined
  }

claims.statement: Past the last step of the journey, Save and continue has no next page to offer.
Pressing Save and continue on a page that is in no journey section raises an error naming the page.
A task row's link opens the first of its pages whose gate passes, and falls back to the row's first page when none does.
The task rows shown under a section are those whose first page sits in that section, ordered by where that page falls in the section.

const firstPageIndexIn = (section, row) =>
  section.pages.findIndex((page) => page.id === row.pages[0].id)

export const taskRowsOfSection = (section) =>
  journeyTaskRows()
    .filter((row) => firstPageIndexIn(section, row) !== -1)
    .sort(
      (rowA, rowB) =>
        firstPageIndexIn(section, rowA) - firstPageIndexIn(section, rowB)
    )

claims.statement: A row's status is worked out in three steps: a row whose condition does not apply reads not applicable; otherwise the row's parts are rolled up into a status; and a rolled-up fulfilled is demoted to in progress when the row's extra answer is still missing.
A row that does not author its own parts counts the obligations its pages collect, so the task list follows the dispatch ownership map by default.

export const rowParts = (row) =>
  row.parts ?? row.pages.flatMap((page) => collectsOf(page.id))

claims.statement: A task row or section reads as one of five statuses: not applicable, not started, in progress, fulfilled or optional.
claims.quote:
export const NA = 'not-applicable'
export const NOT_STARTED = 'not-started'
export const IN_PROGRESS = 'in-progress'
export const FULFILLED = 'fulfilled'
export const OPTIONAL = 'optional'

claims.statement: A row with nothing in scope reads not applicable; a row with no mandatory part reads optional while untouched, then fulfilled or in progress; and a row with mandatory parts reads fulfilled when each is satisfied, in progress when something is started, and not started otherwise.
An empty collection that is required still blocks a row from reading fulfilled, and an empty collection that is optional reads optional while a partly filled optional one reads in progress.
claims.quote:
so the presentation-facing edge cases (empty optional collection -> OPTIONAL,
 * partial optional -> IN_PROGRESS, empty required collection -> NOT_STARTED)
 * hold.
...
 * The empty-collection floor is manifest-sourced (`requiredAtLeastOne`:
 * `requires.minEntries` or `requires.anyOfIds`) and stays a presentation
 * rule — the model emits nothing for a group with zero records, but an
 * empty required collection must still block FULFILLED.

claims.statement: A section's status rolls up every obligation its pages collect, in page order.
claims.quote:
export const sectionObligationIds = (section) =>
  section.pages.flatMap((page) => collectsOf(page.id))

export const sectionStatus = (section, answers, inScope, evaluation) =>
  statusOf(sectionObligationIds(section), answers, inScope, evaluation)

claims.statement: Three of the 52 obligations are groups that hold others inside them: the commodity lines, the animal identifier records inside a line, and the documents.

claims.statement: The country of origin is always asked and always mandatory.
The country-of-origin subdivision code is always in scope and always optional.
Whether a region-of-origin code is required is itself always asked and mandatory.

The region-of-origin code is always in scope, and it switches from optional to mandatory when the trader answers yes to whether a region code is required; the reason given is that a region code is required.
claims.note: This is the only gate in the set that keeps an obligation in scope on both branches, so the answer is never purged when the requirement flips to no.

claims.statement: The arrival date at the port is always asked and always mandatory.
The port of entry is always asked and always mandatory.
The transporter type is always asked and always mandatory.
The commercial transporter record is asked, and mandatory, only when the transporter type is Commercial, and a stored commercial transporter is dropped when the type is switched away from Commercial.
The private transporter record is asked, and mandatory, only when the transporter type is Private, and goes out of scope otherwise.
The commercial and private transporter records are mutually exclusive: only one of the two can be in scope for any transporter type.
claims.quote: // Transporter type + mutually-exclusive address blocks

claims.statement: The means of transport is always asked and always mandatory.
The transport identification is always asked and always mandatory.
The transport document reference is always asked and always mandatory.

The countries transited are asked of rail and road consignments only, and even then they are never compulsory: a trader who passes through nowhere they can name leaves the list empty, the row reads Optional and submission is not held up.
claims.note: An existing ruling: the comment records it as a design release 1 decision.

claims.statement: A conditional obligation whose in-scope decision names no mandate is treated as mandatory, so an optional conditional answer must say 'optional' outright.
claims.quote:
// `status` must say 'optional' outright — `effectiveStatus` falls back to
// 'mandatory' for an implication that carries none.

claims.statement: The place of origin is always asked and always mandatory, and is stored as one composite address record.
The consignor is always asked and always mandatory.
The consignee is always asked and always mandatory.
The importer is always asked and always mandatory.
The place of destination is always asked and always mandatory.
The reason for import is always asked and always mandatory.
The purpose in the internal market is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is internalMarket, and any stored purpose is dropped when the reason changes.
The destination country is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is transit or transhipmentOrOnwardTravel, and is otherwise out of scope and purged.
claims.note: An existing ruling: the code records the V4 data dictionary (Confluence page 6497338582) as the authority for this rule.

claims.statement: The port of exit is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is transit or temporaryAdmissionHorses, and is chosen from the same port list as the port of entry.
The exit date is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is temporaryAdmissionHorses, and is otherwise out of scope and purged.
The contact address is always asked and always mandatory.
The internal reference number is trader-entered, always in scope and always optional.
What the animals are certified for is asked once for the whole notification and is always mandatory, although the spec notes APHA may make it depend on the commodity later.
The notification's approved reference number is assigned by the system when the notification is created and is never entered by a trader; it is mandatory but no page asks for it.
The notification's reference number is shaped GBN-AG-YY-XXXXXX, where the six-character body uses Crockford base32 (0-9 and A-Z without I, L, O or U).
A notification must hold at least one commodity line, and an empty list is refused under the code obligation.commodityLine.atLeastOne.
claims.note: The commodity lines group states no upper limit on the number of lines.

claims.statement: Every commodity line must carry a commodity code.
Every commodity line must carry a species Latin name.
A commodity line's species common name is optional.
Every commodity line must carry a number of animals.
A line's number of packages is asked only when that line's commodity code is in the package-count list, and even then it is optional.
The county parish holding number is asked, and mandatory, when any commodity line's code is in the CPH-required list, and is out of scope otherwise.
Whether the consignment contains unweaned animals is asked once for the whole notification, and only when any commodity line's code is in the unweaned list.

Each animal identifier record inside a commodity line must carry at least one of seven identifiers: a microchip, a passport, a tattoo, an ear tag, a horse name, identification details or a description; an empty record is refused under obligation.unitRecord.identifiersRequired.

The at-least-one-identifier floor is stood down unless more than one commodity line has a code in the identified list, so a consignment with a single identified line is not held to it at the collection level.
claims.quote:
floorAppliesToParent: moreThanOne(
      allowListed(commodityCode, identifiedCommodityCodes, null)
    )
---
 * The inner gate names the entries that would be asked; this wrapper stands
 * the whole rule down unless there are at least two of them, and otherwise
 * hands back the inner decision untouched with the same `fulfilmentIndexes`.
claims.note: mechanism: works on the commodity-lines collection. moreThanOne returns the inner allowListed decision only when it admits more than one entry, and otherwise reports out of scope.

claims.statement: A microchip is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the microchip list, and is optional there.
A passport is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the passport list, and is optional there.
A tattoo is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the tattoo list, and is optional there.
An ear tag is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the ear-tag list, and is optional there.
A horse name is asked of an animal only when its line's commodity code and species Latin name together are in the horse-name list, and is optional there.
claims.quote:
export const horseName = {
  id: HORSE_NAME_ID,
  name: 'horseName',
  within: unitRecord,
  status: 'optional',
  applyTo: allowListedPairs(
    commodityCode,
    speciesLatinName,
    horseNameCodeSpecies,
    unitRecord,
    [horseNameReason]
  )
}

claims.statement: Identification details are asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is outside the identified list, and are optional there.
A free-text description is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is outside the identified list, and is optional there.
A permanent address is asked of an animal, and is mandatory, when its line's commodity code and species pair is in the permanent-address list.
claims.quote:
const permanentAddressPairGate = (reasons) =>
  allowListedPairs(
    commodityCode,
    speciesLatinName,
    permanentAddressCodeSpecies,
    unitRecord,
    reasons
  )

export const permanentAddress = {
  id: '3fcbd0e6-f708-4c2c-89ab-a56c7e8ea0b7',
  name: 'permanentAddress',
  within: unitRecord,
  status: 'mandatory',
  applyTo: permanentAddressPairGate([permanentAddressReason])
}
claims.note: The only mandatory per-animal identifier obligation; every other one is optional.

claims.statement: Where that permanent address came from is asked on the same animals as the permanent address itself, and is optional.
claims.quote:

  id: '4e1f2a3b-5c6d-4f70-8e81-9f2a3b4c5d6e',

claims.statement: A trader can attach between zero and fifteen accompanying documents to a notification, and a sixteenth is refused under obligation.accompanyingDocument.tooMany.
The fifteen-document cap is enforced on the stored notification as well as on the page's Add affordance, so a saved notification holding more than the cap is still caught afterwards.
Each accompanying document must carry its own type, attachment type, reference and date of issue; all four are mandatory within a document.
A document's upload id and filename are optional, so a document can be recorded without a file attached.
The V4 data dictionary page still reads as if a notification can hold at most one accompanying document, and the obligation model is treated as the authority until that page is amended.
claims.note: An existing ruling recorded in code: a known disagreement with the V4 source, resolved in favour of the model.

claims.statement: Each document's instance id is a session-scoped counter value such as doc1 or doc2.
claims.quote: // Instance ids are session-scoped counter values (`doc1`, `doc2`, …).

claims.statement: A gate that reads one stored answer and swaps the mandate keeps the answer in scope on both branches, while one that swaps in scope drops the stored answer when the gate answer flips.
claims.quote:
Both
 * `whenTrue` and `whenFalse` are returned verbatim, so a caller who
 * passes two in-scope decisions gets a pure status flip (e.g.
 * `regionCode` mandatory ↔ optional), and one in-scope + one
 * out-of-scope gets a purge-on-flip (e.g. `purposeInInternalMarket`
 * dropped when `reasonForImport` changes).

claims.statement: A per-line or per-animal gate decides entry by entry, so one commodity line can be asked for an identifier while another in the same consignment is not.
claims.quote:
/**
 * allowListed — in scope on entries where `gateObligation`'s stored
 * value is in the allowlist.
 *
 * - Depth-1 (gate + gated at the same identity level): pass `null` for
 *   `gatedParentGroup`; fulfilmentIndexes are the passing gate keys.
 * - Depth-N > 1 (gate broader than gated): pass the gated obligation's
 *   parent group as `gatedParentGroup`; fulfilmentIndexes are that
 *   group's fulfilmentIndexes whose ancestor prefix has a passing gate.

claims.statement: An answer that is blank never counts as outside an allowlist, so a commodity line with no code yet is not treated as an unidentified species.
claims.quote:
/**
 * notInUnionOf — dual of `allowListed`. In scope on entries whose
 * `gateObligation` stored value is not blank and not in the union of the
 * given allowlists. The union is derived at call-time and exposed on
 * `.metadata.values`.

 */

claims.statement: The commodity search asks the reference data service for GET /commodities with the search term as q and the page and size as query parameters.
The species check asks the reference data service for POST /commodities/species-check with the commodity lines in the body.
claims.quote:

  requestReferenceData(
    referenceDataUrl('/commodities/species-check'),
    { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ lines }) },
    'Failed to check species'

claims.statement: The species check returns the commodity lines whose Latin name is not listed under their commodity code, and an empty list when every line's species is listed.
claims.quote:
/**
 * @param {Array<{code: string, latinName: string}>} lines - the lines to check.
 * @returns {Promise<Array<{code: string, latinName: string}>>} the lines whose

 * @throws {import('@hapi/boom').Boom} 503 when reference data fails.

claims.statement: No species check is made at all when there are no commodity lines to check.
A species-check reply that carries no unlisted list is treated as a failure rather than as 'nothing unlisted'.

When the service is run in stub mode both the commodity search and the species check are answered from the service's own fixtures instead of reference data, and stub mode is never honoured in production.
A reference data failure is turned into a 503 'Reference data unavailable' naming the dataset that failed, either 'commodities' or 'species'.
Every call to reference data carries the service's trace headers and a JSON content type, and any non-OK reply is raised as a failure carrying the status, status text and URL.

Six commodity codes carry per-animal identifiers: cattle 0102 (ear tag, passport, tattoo), horses 0101 (microchip, passport and a horse name for Equus cabalus), swine 0103 (ear tag, tattoo), sheep 010410 (ear tag), goats 010420 (ear tag) and other live mammals 01061900 (microchip, passport, tattoo).
Those same six codes are the identified list, so a commodity line with any other code is treated as unidentified and asked for identification details and a description instead.
claims.quote: export const IDENTIFIED_CODES = Object.keys(COMMODITY_IDENTIFIERS)

Horses (0101) ask for a package count but do not require a CPH number; the three 0407 egg codes require a CPH number but ask for no package count.

claims.note: Cats, dogs and ferrets, in Latin.

claims.statement: Four commodity codes carry a description: 0101 'Live horses, asses, mules and hinnies', 0102 'Live bovine animals', 01061900 'Other live animals' and 0301 'Live fish'.
Three commodity codes carry a short name: 0101 'Horse', 0102 'Cattle' and 0301 'Fish'.
Live fish, commodity code 0301, has a description and a short name but no identifiers, so a fish consignment is asked for identification details and a description rather than a tag or passport.
claims.quote: export const LIVE_FISH_CODE = '0301'
claims.note: 0301 is absent from COMMODITY_IDENTIFIERS, so it is outside IDENTIFIED_CODES and the notInUnionOf gates for identification details and description admit it.

claims.statement: The per-identifier code lists are derived from the one identifier table rather than written out, so a code that carries an identifier is always in that identifier's list.
claims.note: mechanism: turns the identifier table into per-identifier code lists, and into code-and-species pairs for an identifier that names a species.

claims.statement: A commodity search in stub mode matches a group when the term is a prefix of its CN code, and otherwise matches a species when every word of the term is a prefix of consecutive words of its Latin or common name.
claims.note: mechanism: the stub's own matching over the captured commodity fixtures; an empty term matches nothing by name, and a code prefix match returns the group's whole species list.

claims.statement: Stub search results are paged by slicing the flattened matches and then regrouping them by code, so a group can be split across two pages and the total counts species rather than groups.
claims.note: mechanism: paging over the stub's flattened code-and-species matches.

claims.statement: In stub mode a commodity line counts as unlisted when the captured fixtures hold no group with that code carrying that exact Latin name.
claims.quote:
const listedInStub = ({ code, latinName }) =>
  COMMODITY_GROUPS.some(
    (group) =>
      group.code === code &&
      group.species.some((species) => species.latinName === latinName)
  )

export const unlistedLinesInStub = (lines) =>
  lines.filter((line) => !listedInStub(line))

claims.statement: Four answers decide which conditional questions a trader sees, and they are exercised as a cross product of 48 states: whether a region code is required, the reason for import (unanswered, internal market, transit or temporary admission of horses), the means of transport (unanswered or road vehicle) and the transporter type (unanswered, commercial or private).
claims.quote:
/**
 * The scope-determining flags whose cross-product spans the conditional
 * obligations moving into and out of scope: the region-code requirement, the
 * import reason, the means of transport and the transporter type. The reason
 * axis carries transit and temporary-admission values so the reason-gated
 * destinationCountry / portOfExit / exitDate obligations are exercised.
 * 2×4×2×3 = 48 states.
 *
 * @returns {Array<object>} 48 partial answer states.
 */

claims.statement: The journey's reachability is proved over 240 answer states, each of the five seed variants overlaid with each of the 48 scope states, with unanswered values left out rather than stored blank.
claims.note: 5 seed variants × 48 scope states = 240 answer states.

claims.statement: Two answers are the required earlier answers every later page needs before it will open: the country of origin and at least one commodity line.
claims.note: Matches the two obligations named in ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE, countryOfOrigin and commodityCode.

claims.statement: The return carries four things in its query: fulfilment-id, handshake-token, addressId and landing.
The landing the address book names may be one of three: select, return or cancel.
A return naming a fulfilment id the service does not know is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Unknown fulfilment', and the refusal is logged as 'Address return refused'.
A return naming a landing that is not select, return or cancel is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Unknown landing'.
A return that names a landing other than cancel but no address is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Missing address'.
A return that names no landing at all but does carry an address is treated as a selection.
A return that names neither a landing nor an address — someone simply coming back — takes the trader to that party's address picker, saves nothing and needs no handshake token.
claims.note: The token check comes after this branch, so a bare return is always honoured.

claims.statement: Every other return must carry the handshake token the service issued for that fulfilment id, and one that does not is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Invalid handshake'.
claims.note: Security: this is the check that stops a return being replayed or forged for a party the trader never started a hand-off for. The token is compared against the trader's own cookie, so a return cannot be honoured in someone else's session.

claims.statement: A handshake token is used once: it is forgotten as soon as the return is accepted, and the whole cookie is dropped once no hand-off is outstanding.
A trader who cancels in the address book is returned to the notification overview, and nothing is saved.

An address returned as a selection is read back from the address book, copied onto the party as its answer, and the trader is taken to that party's return page — the Consignment addresses page for all five consignment parties — with the added-address banner naming it.
An address returned with the 'return' landing is read back and the banner is shown, but it is not saved onto the party: the trader is taken to that party's address picker to choose it there.
claims.note: So 'select' means the address book chose the party's address for the trader, and 'return' means it only added the address to the book.

people to reach for `--no-verify`, which skips the cheap format and lint
checks as well. A push is the first point the work affects anyone else, so
the gate sits there.

claims.statement: The repo records that installing dependencies installs both git hooks, because postinstall runs the husky set-up script.

claims.statement: The repo records that the same pre-push gate can be run by hand at any time with npm run git:pre-push-hook, or just its fast half with npm run git:pre-push-checks.

claims.note: Unclaimed: the extract records what pre-push runs and why it sits there, but not that the gate is runnable on demand, nor that there is a named fast-half script.

claims.statement: The repo records that the workspace's pre-push gate runs its cheap checks before the build, so a formatting slip fails in seconds instead of after a full suite.

That gate runs the cheap checks before the build,

claims.note: Unclaimed: the ordering decision inside the workspace gate, which is the reason the skip marker is cheap to earn, sits between the two halves of claim repo-frontend-p19-432's ref and neither claim records it.

claims.statement: The repo records that the application is run locally in development mode with npm run dev, and that npm start mimics it running in production mode locally.

claims.note: Unclaimed. The production half is at README.md:185-189: "To mimic the application running in `production` mode locally run:" then `npm start`.

claims.statement: The repo records that it builds two Docker images — a development image built with the development target and a production image built with no target — each run on port 3000, with an Apple Silicon note that a platform flag may be needed.

claims.statement: A submission event is published under the event type NotificationSubmitted, with a schema version and a schema URL under schemas.defra.gov.uk naming the event and its version.

An outbox event can carry the actor who caused it — an id, a source, a user type, a display name, an organisation id and an organisation acted on behalf of — and a list of status changes, each a status, the date it changed and the actor who changed it.
The notification published to other services is a GBN-AG document with two halves: an exchanged document and a specified consignment.

The published exchanged document carries the notification's identifier, the trader's own assigned id, a notification status code, a version id, an issue date and time, the issuer, a list of signed clauses, and a list of referenced documents.

The published specified consignment carries the consignor, consignee, despatch, delivery, importer and carrier parties, the origin country, the unloading base port, the final destination, the main carriage transport movements, the transit countries, whether the consignment holds unweaned animals, and the consignment items.

A published trade line item carries a description, the scientific and common species names, a product unit quantity per delivery, an item quantity per package, and the individual animals, each with a name and a list of identifiers.
Each animal identifier is published as a type code and a content value, so the kind of identifier (ear tag, passport and so on) travels as a code beside the number.
claims.note: notification-data-gaps.spec.ts:86 and :120 name EAR_TAG and PASSPORT as two of those type codes.

claims.statement: A published party carries an identifier, a URL id, a name, a party role code and a list of party type codes, each coded value being a value with an optional URL id and name.

A published country carries a code, its subordinate country sub-divisions and a region of origin code; a published location carries an identifier, a URL id, a name and a type code; and a published transport movement carries a numeric mode code and the transport contract documents.

The canned submission event the suite keeps carries a flat summary of the notification — reference number, status, point of entry and a commodities list of species name and number of animals — not the GBN-AG document the outbox event model describes.

The flow helpers wait for each page's heading with `pageLoadWait`
(`config/timeouts.ts`, 30s) rather than the test timeout, so a transient 502
fails the step that hit it within 30s and names the page it was waiting for.

claims.statement: Sign-in waits for either the landing page or the "Sorry, we are unable to sign you in." page before deciding whether to try again.
claims.quote:
Sign-in waits for either the landing page or the "Sorry, we are unable to sign
you in." page before deciding whether to try again.

claims.statement: The address-book fixtures delete every address and transporter created through them when the test ends, pass or fail and on every retry, and a delete that fails is logged with the record's id and never fails the test.
claims.quote:
The `addressBookApi` and `isolatedOrganisationAddressBookApi` fixtures delete
every address and transporter created through them once the test ends, pass or
fail, retries included.

claims.statement: A transporter saved through the user interface is only deleted if the spec tracks it by name, and an address added on the add-address page or through the handshake is not deleted at all.
claims.quote:
A record a test saves through the UI is not created
through them: call `addressBookApi.trackTransporterNamed(name)` after saving a
transporter so it is deleted too. A delete that fails is logged with the
record's id and never fails the test. Records saved through the UI in any other
way, such as an address added on the add-address page or through the
handshake, are not deleted.

claims.statement: In CDP dev, test, perf-test and ext-test the address book removes every address about seven days after it was created, which needs both ADDRESS_TTL_DAYS and ADDRESS_TTL_EXPIRY_ENABLED set; the local docker-compose stack sets neither.

In CDP dev, test, perf-test and ext-test the address book also removes every
address about 7 days after it was created. That needs both `ADDRESS_TTL_DAYS`
and `ADDRESS_TTL_EXPIRY_ENABLED` set; the local docker-compose stack sets
neither.

claims.statement: Every address or transporter name a test creates carries a timestamp or UUID suffix so a search finds only that run's record.
claims.quote:
Make each name unique (a timestamp or UUID suffix) so a search finds
only this run's record.

claims.statement: The shared journey addresses are seeded in global set-up through its own client, so no test's clean-up deletes them, and where expiry is on the next run's set-up creates them again.
claims.quote:
Where expiry is on, the shared journey addresses
seeded in `globalSetup` expire too; the next run's `ensureE2eAddressBook`
creates them again. `globalSetup` seeds them through its own client, so no
test's clean-up deletes them.

claims.statement: A spec that edits or deletes an address makes its own record rather than using a shared journey address, because every spec running alongside it reads those.
claims.quote:
A spec that edits or deletes an address makes its own record rather than
using one of the shared journey addresses, because every spec running
alongside it reads those.

claims.statement: The address book checks only that a country is present, so a record whose country is a country name rather than a listed code is the one way through the services alone to copy an address the notification refuses.

A spec that checks a copied address against the

than a listed code: the address book checks only that a country is present,

claims.quote: `@duplicated-in-frontend` marks an end-to-end spec whose behaviour the frontend's own FIT suite also proves, so a reader knows the check exists in both places.

claims.statement: The suite does not wipe the database before it runs and does not need to, because every spec creates the state it asserts on through the back-end API, scoped to that run, so the specs pass against a database holding earlier runs' records.

Every spec creates the state it asserts on through the front door (the
backend API), scoped to that run, so the specs pass against a database that
already holds the records of earlier runs.

claims.statement: A spec asserts which journey page is open through the page object's expected URL pattern, which matches the page whichever trail its address carries, and asserts an exact trail through the on-trail pattern or exact URL built from the page objects' own slugs; a spec never types a from query itself.
claims.quote:
- Which page is open: the page object's `expectedUrlPattern(reference)`. It matches the page whichever trail its address carries.
- The exact trail: the page object's `expectedUrlPatternOnTrail(reference, places)` for a `toHaveURL` matcher, or `expectedUrlOnTrail(reference, places)` for an exact `href` value. Pass the page objects' own `slug`s and the `TRAIL_START` places. A spec never types a `?from=` query.

claims.statement: Visual regression tests guard rendered composition — layout, spacing, colour and typography as the user sees the page — by comparing screenshots against committed baseline images and failing if any pixels differ outside the masked regions.
claims.quote: Visual regression tests (tagged `@visual`) guard rendered composition — layout, spacing, colour, and typography as the user sees the page. They compare screenshots against committed baseline images and fail if any pixels differ outside the masked regions.

claims.statement: Baselines are committed beside their spec files, and each platform needs its own baseline, both of which are updated when a visual change is intentional.
claims.quote: Baselines are stored alongside their spec files in `*-snapshots/` directories and must be committed. Each platform requires its own baseline — update both when visual changes are intentional.

claims.statement: Visual specs run headless whatever the project setting, because headed mode uses the operating system's font rendering, which produces pixel differences against a headless baseline.
claims.quote: Visual specs run headless whatever the project setting, because headed mode uses OS font rendering, which produces pixel differences against a headless baseline.

claims.statement: On macOS a visual run launches the browser itself with legacy scroll bars, because Chromium sizes a native select's arrow box from the macOS scroll bar style and overlay scroll bars draw every native select four pixels narrower, which failed a baseline made on a trackpad once a mouse was plugged in.
claims.quote: Visual specs import `test` from `@fixtures/visual`. On macOS it launches Playwright's headless shell with legacy scroll bars (`-AppleShowScrollBars Always`) and connects to it over CDP. Chromium sizes a native `<select>` arrow box from the macOS scroll bar style, and with the default "Show scroll bars: Automatically" setting that style follows whether a mouse is connected: overlay scroll bars on a trackpad alone, legacy ones with a mouse. Overlay scroll bars draw every native select 4px narrower, so a `*-darwin.png` baseline made on a laptop's trackpad failed with a mouse plugged in (704 pixels on the no-JavaScript import reason page), and the other way round. Playwright's own launch refuses an argument that does not start with `-`, so the fixture starts the browser itself. On Linux the fixture is the shared one, unchanged.
claims.note: mechanism: the visual fixture's own browser launch, for the macOS baseline. Names the no-JavaScript import reason page as the page whose baseline differed.

claims.statement: The declaration visual specs set the date of declaration to a fixed string before the screenshot rather than masking it, because the server writes today's date into the page text and a mask is as wide as that text; the date's strong emphasis is proved by the declaration end-to-end specs instead.
claims.quote: The declaration specs set the date of declaration to a fixed string before the screenshot instead of masking it, because the server writes today's date into the page text and a mask is as wide as that text, which changes with the day and month. `freezeDatePickersAt` does not reach that text: it stops the browser clock and moves each date picker's served bounds, and changes nothing the server has already written. The date's strong emphasis is proved by the declaration e2e specs.

claims.statement: Only the animals and plants domains have visual specs.
claims.quote: `animals` and `plants` have `@visual` specs.

claims.statement: Baselines are regenerated by two commands, one for the host-rendered darwin image and one for the container-rendered linux image CI uses, each running every visual spec and writing the updated snapshot into the working tree for commit.
claims.quote:
Regenerate the E2E baseline against the stack frontend with
`npm run test:visual:update:macos` for the host-rendered `*-darwin.png` image and
`npm run test:visual:update:linux` for the container-rendered `*-linux.png` image
used by CI. Both commands run every `@visual` spec and write the
updated snapshot into the working tree for commit.

claims.statement: The Linux baseline script points the service URLs at host.docker.internal and maps localhost to the host, because inside the container localhost is the container.
claims.quote: The Linux script points the service URLs at `host.docker.internal`, because inside the container `localhost` is the container. It also runs the container with `--add-host=localhost:host-gateway`, which maps `localhost` to the host, so any URL the script does not override and that still names `localhost` reaches the stack too.

claims.statement: Every full-page screenshot of a notification page masks the whole status strip, not the reference alone, so the masked box stays a fixed size while the notification reference is minted per run; the strip's own content is covered by an end-to-end spec.
claims.quote:
Every full-page screenshot of a notification page masks the whole status strip. It renders
from the first request and holds the notification reference, which is minted per run. The
whole strip is masked, not the reference alone, so the masked box stays a fixed size. The
strip's own content is covered by `tests/animals/e2e/features/reference-strip.spec.ts`.

claims.statement: A calendar screenshot depends on today's date twice — the browser's today picks the month and highlighted day, and the server's today sets each picker's minimum and maximum date — so the suite stops the browser clock on a fixed day and moves the served bounds by the same number of days.
claims.quote:
A calendar screenshot depends on today's date twice: the browser's today picks the month and
the highlighted day, and the server's today sets each picker's `data-min-date` and

claims.statement: A cross-browser command names its project explicitly and adds the tag filter, because without the filter a named engine would run every test.
claims.quote: - The commands add `--grep '@cross-browser'`. Without it a named engine runs every test.

claims.statement: Branded Chrome is installed in the amd64 test image only, because Google publishes no Linux Arm64 build, and is installed from Google locally rather than through Playwright, whose install would replace the browser already there.
claims.quote: - `chrome` launches the installed Google Chrome. The amd64 test image installs it (Google publishes no Linux Arm64 build); locally, install it from Google. Do not run `npx playwright install chrome` on your own machine: it replaces the browser you already have.

claims.statement: On an iPhone user agent the accessible autocomplete adds a hidden position counter to each suggestion, so the type-ahead helper accepts an optional position suffix, and a spec must not assume a fixed viewport.
claims.quote:
- On an iPhone user agent, `accessible-autocomplete` adds a hidden "1 of 7" to each suggestion, so `TypeAhead.option()` accepts an optional position suffix.
- Specs must not assume a fixed viewport.

claims.statement: The BrowserStack run uses the team's service account credentials from the environment, never from the config file.
claims.quote: # Never write credentials here: the SDK reads them from BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME and BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY (.env locally, CDP secrets on CDP).

claims.statement: BrowserStack Local is always on, carrying the docker-compose stack's localhost URLs and CDP's internal hostnames to the remote browser, but Safari, WebKit and Android browsers cannot open localhost through it, so the iOS and macOS platforms run only against CDP.
claims.quote:
- BrowserStack Local is always on. It carries the docker-compose stack's `localhost` URLs, and CDP's hostnames, which resolve only inside the platform, to the remote browser.
- Safari, WebKit and Android browsers cannot open `localhost` through BrowserStack Local, so the iOS and macOS platforms run only on CDP.

claims.statement: Session reuse is off on BrowserStack so every test signs in for itself, because real iPhones allow only one browser context.
claims.quote: - Session reuse is off (`E2E_SESSION_REUSE=off`), so every test signs in for itself: real iPhones allow only one browser context.

claims.statement: Each BrowserStack platform runs half the machine's processors in parallel, up to the team-wide limit of 13 sessions, and that number can be overridden by a setting that must be a positive whole number.
claims.quote: - Each platform runs half your CPUs in parallel, up to the team-wide limit of 13 sessions. Set `BROWSERSTACK_PARALLELS_PER_PLATFORM` to change it.

claims.statement: A BrowserStack build is named local, github or cdp with the environment, identified by the run id or a UTC time, under the project trade-imports-ins-tests, and each run prints its results link.
claims.quote: - Builds are named `local`, `github` or `cdp-<ENVIRONMENT>`, with a UTC time or the run id as the identifier, under the project `trade-imports-ins-tests`.

claims.statement: A BrowserStack run from a laptop or GitHub targets the docker-compose stack, while a CDP run targets the CDP environment, each with its own Playwright config.
GitHub Actions does not run the BrowserStack suite.
claims.quote: The BrowserStack run uses the platforms in [Browsers](#browsers). It runs on CDP, against a CDP environment, and from your machine against the docker-compose stack. GitHub Actions doesn't run it.

claims.statement: BrowserStack network logs are off because they keep every request's headers, sign-in cookies included, on BrowserStack for 30 days; video, interactive debugging, error-level console logs, Playwright logs and test observability are on.
claims.quote:
debug: false
# Off: network logs keep every request's headers, sign-in cookies included, on BrowserStack for 30 days.
networkLogs: false
networkLogsOptions: false
video: true
interactiveDebugging: true
consoleLogs: errors
playwrightLogs: true

claims.statement: When a proxy is set, as on CDP, the BrowserStack SDK writes a CommonJS require into its generated config, which fails in this ES module project, so the run preloads a file defining a global require into the SDK and its workers.
claims.quote: - When a proxy is set (`HTTP_PROXY`, as on CDP), the SDK writes `require("global-agent")` into its generated Playwright config, which fails in an ES module project. `bin/browserstack-global-require.mjs` defines a global `require` for it, and `bin/run-browserstack.ts` preloads that file into the SDK and its workers.

claims.statement: A BrowserStack run stops before starting if either credential is missing, naming both.

    process.exit(1);

claims.statement: The dependency audit is a separate job from the pull-request checks, so a newly published advisory does not become the check that gates the merge and does not block the pull request carrying the fix.

# Deliberately a separate job from cdp-workflows. The audit (audit-ci over
