claims.statement: Every audit allowlist entry must be keyed by a GHSA id, be active, carry notes giving a reason and an owner, and have a real expiry date no more than three months away; an expired entry is named as expired and fails the check, and the weekly run catches expiries between pull requests.
claims.quote:
# Before the audit, "Check audit allowlist" enforces the allowlist rules:
  # every entry is {"GHSA-...": {active: true, notes, expiry}}, the notes give
  # a reason and "Owner: <name>", and the expiry is a real date no more than
  # 3 months away. An expired entry is named as EXPIRED, which audit-ci alone
  # does not say. The weekly cron catches expiries between PRs.

claims.statement: A push to main builds the test image and publishes it to both the CDP container registry and Docker Hub, tagged with the computed next version and latest, labelled with the repo, the test suite name, the build run id and the commit, and then commits the version tag.

]

claims.statement: The suite keeps its support code in named folders: the specs under tests, multi-page sequences under flows, one class per page under page-objects, shared constants and models under domain, Playwright fixtures, HTTP, MongoDB and SQS clients under adapters, canned data under resources, and cross-domain helpers under utils.
claims.quote: | `flows/<domain>` | Multi-page sequences: `journey.ts` `to*` methods and the actions built on them              |

claims.statement: A spec reaches a page through a named step in its domain's journey file rather than through its own clicks, and a sequence used by two tests becomes such a step with the local copies deleted.
claims.quote:
- A spec reaches a page through a `to*` method in `flows/<domain>/journey.ts`, not through its own clicks.
- A sequence used by two tests becomes a `to*` method in that file. Delete the local copies when you add it.

claims.statement: A journey spec is never seeded: seeding is only for the set-up of a one-page assertion, and everything else is walked through the pages.
claims.quote: - Never seed a journey spec. Seed only the set-up for a one-page assertion; walk everything else through the pages.

claims.statement: Test data is copied from real canned data — the service's fixtures, the reference data or the stub — and never invented.
claims.quote: - Copy test data from real canned data (the service's fixtures, reference data, the stub). Never invent it.

claims.statement: A test run is never piped: it is redirected to a file and the file is read.
claims.quote: - Never pipe a test run. Redirect it to a file and read the file.

claims.statement: The animals journey's answers are plain data held apart from the steps that drive the pages, and come in named sets: a mandatory set where a missing answer is a compile error, and a full set.
claims.quote:
- `journey.ts` drives pages. Notification answers, what a user says, are plain data in `domain/animals/constants/journey-options.ts`.
- Answers come in named sets: the mandatory set (a missing answer is a compile error) and the full set.

claims.statement: A spec starts from an answer set and overrides single values only where the test needs them, and never changes the journey steps to get a different value.
claims.quote: A spec starts from a set and overrides single values only where the test needs them, e.g. `{ ...MANDATORY_ANSWERS, unweanedAnimals: yesNoValues.yes }`. It never changes `journey.ts` to get a different value.

claims.statement: An answer states a fact and never how it is entered, so the user interface and the seeded journeys build from the same answers by default, and a new field touches one answer type and the step that enters it.
claims.quote:
- An answer states a fact, never how it is entered. By default the UI and seeded journeys build from the same answers.
- A new field touches one answer type and the step that enters it.

claims.statement: The plants journey's answers live in the plants journey file rather than in a separate constants file as animals' do.
claims.quote: - Plants answers live in `flows/plants/journey.ts`.

claims.statement: A test title states what its assertions prove, and a test must fail without the change it covers.
claims.quote: - A test title states what its assertions prove. A test must fail without the change it covers.

claims.statement: Lint, the formatting check and the type check are run before a commit.
claims.quote: Run `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run typecheck`.

claims.statement: A pre-commit hook checks lint and formatting on staged files only and blocks the commit if the checks fail.
claims.quote: This project uses **Husky** and **lint-staged** to automatically validate code quality before commits. The pre-commit hook checks linting (ESLint) and formatting (Prettier) on staged files only. If checks fail, the commit is blocked.

claims.statement: A single test's timeout is raised with a helper that, in debug mode, leaves a test with no timeout at all.
claims.quote: Raise the run-wide timeout in `playwright.config.ts`. Raise a single test's timeout with `setTestTimeout` from `@utils/playwright/test-timeout`, which leaves a test with no timeout, as in debug mode, with none.

claims.statement: A brand-new animals notification first shows the origin of import page with nothing answered.
claims.quote: - `toOriginOfImport` shows origin unanswered, as a brand-new notification first shows it.

claims.statement: The notification's entry guard admits a notification on an answer the user entered, so opening the overview before origin is saved shows origin again.
claims.quote: - `createNotificationAtOrigin` ends on the origin page with nothing answered. The entry guard admits a notification on an answer the user entered, so opening its overview before origin is saved shows origin again.

claims.statement: A task left at "Not yet started" on the overview is what a failed save of the origin page shows up as, several steps later.
claims.quote: - `startNotification` waits for the origin page to leave before it opens the overview. Opening the overview regardless hides a failed save: the run then fails several steps later on a task stuck at "Not yet started", pointing at the wrong page.

claims.statement: The arrival date must fall inside a window from one week back to six months ahead, and the application renders a date in unpadded day/month/four-digit-year form.
claims.quote: - `ARRIVAL_DATE` (in `domain/animals/constants/journey-options.ts`) falls inside the arrival-date window (one week back to six months ahead) wherever the wall clock is, written in the unpadded d/m/yyyy the application renders. A check-your-answers assertion then compares against the application's shape, not the typed string it echoes back.

claims.statement: A temporary admission's exit date falls after the arrival date.
claims.quote: - `TEMPORARY_ADMISSION_EXIT_DATE` falls after the arrival date, in the same format.

claims.statement: An accompanying document is added by waiting for the virus scan to finish, so the submission carries the document.
claims.quote: - `uploadDocumentAndWaitForScan` waits for the virus scan to finish so the submission carries the document.

claims.statement: A document list is expected within ten seconds and a virus scan within 90 seconds, the scan ceiling being sized for CDP's real scanner at about 30 seconds on the test virus file while the local stub settles on its first refresh read.
The suite's shared waiting budgets are one second, five seconds, ten seconds, 30 seconds, 60 seconds and 120 seconds.
A submitted notification is given only the answers the frontend requires unless a fuller set is passed.
claims.quote: - `submitNotification` gives only the answers the frontend requires (`MANDATORY_ANSWERS`), unless the caller passes a fuller set such as `ALL_ANSWERS`.

claims.statement: The import reason's purpose is a conditional reveal under the reason, so both answers are submitted together.
claims.quote: - The import reason's purpose is a conditional reveal under the reason, so both answers go in on one submit.

claims.statement: The transporter page saves through unfilled, and the default means of transport, Road, keeps transited countries in scope, with transit countries answered next.
claims.quote: - `reachTransporterFromHub` goes back to the transporter list from the hub within a journey that is already unlocked. The page saves through unfilled. Arrival details are filled on the way because the default means, Road, keeps transited countries in scope, and transit countries are answered next.

claims.statement: A transporter is added from the transporter list by answering a transporter type question, and the commercial arm goes list, then type question, then a form for a commercial transporter that is not on the list.
claims.quote: - `toCommercialTransporter` follows the add route's commercial arm: the list first, then the transporter type question, then the form for a commercial transporter that is not on the list.

claims.statement: Saving a private transporter's add form lands back on the transporter list with the new transporter first and chosen.
claims.quote: - `fillAndSavePrivateTransporterAddForm` fills the open private transporter form with the details given and saves it, waiting for the transporter list the save lands back on with the new transporter first and chosen.

claims.statement: Saving a commercial transporter's form lands on the transporter list, and saving that list reaches the overview.
claims.quote: - `fillAndSaveCommercialTransporterAddFormToOverview` fills and saves the open commercial transporter form, then saves the transporter list it lands on, reaching the overview — the one path specs that only need the overview, not the list's own state, take through the save.

claims.statement: The transporter list shows only the newest address-book entry of each name, so when two tests add a transporter of the same name at once the later add replaces the entry the earlier test's list chose, and that list's save is refused with "Select a transporter from the list".

When two tests add a transporter of the same name at once, the later add replaces the entry the earlier test's list chose, and that list's save is refused with "Select a transporter from the list".

claims.statement: The overview lists one set of task rows for a consignment that identifies an animal and travels by air or sea and another for an overland consignment, each in a fixed order the assertion exists to prove.
claims.quote: - `OVERLAND_OVERVIEW_TASKS` is the overview's task rows for an overland consignment, in the order the overview lists them. It is stated outright rather than derived from `AIR_OR_SEA_OVERVIEW_TASKS`, because the order is what the assertion that reads it exists to prove.

claims.statement: A rail consignment in transit passes the identification page with both of the chosen commodity's free-text fallback answers blank, because that commodity declares no identifier of its own and the two answers are optional.

claims.statement: The permanent address page is reached from the consignment addresses page, inside the leg of the journey that runs from the transporter to the review.

claims.statement: The animals API seed unlocks only origin and commodity, so a spec that needs the review walks the whole journey rather than seeding it.
claims.quote: - The API seed unlocks only origin and commodity, so a spec that needs the review walks the whole journey rather than seeding it. The walk's addresses leg picks the canned parties whose names and countries a review assertion reads.

claims.statement: A party picker refuses an address-book record that does not carry the role the picker is for, so each role's answer must name a record holding that role.
claims.quote: - `PartyNames` (`flows/animals/seed-form-steps.ts`) names the address-book record each role's answer picks. Every name must match a record `flows/shared/address-book-seed.ts` seeds holding that role, since a picker now refuses a record that does not carry its own role.

claims.statement: A party picker only threads its checked party through a server round trip, so a link off the page before that round trip carries the previously-saved party rather than the just-ticked one.
claims.quote: - `selectAndCommit` (`page-objects/animals/party-picker-page.ts`) ticks a party's radio, then re-searches to commit it: the picker only threads its checked party through a server round trip, so a link off the page before that round trip carries the previously-saved party, not the just-ticked one.

claims.statement: On the notification view a party's summary-list row is found by the card's title with the role as the row's term.

claims.statement: A summary card on the notification view offers a heading Change link and may offer a row link such as Edit details, and a card can hold a titled subsection such as "Permanent address" with its own summary list.

claims.statement: A summary list has no error state of its own, so an outstanding role carries its message in the row's value cell.
claims.quote: - `partyError` reads the first definition of the row. A summary list has no error state of its own, so an outstanding role carries its message in the row's value cell.

claims.statement: The workspace stack is started from published images, built from local source, stopped with its volumes wiped, or have its backend rebuilt, by four workspace commands the suite documents.
claims.quote:
| `tim docker up`             | Start the full stack from published images             |
| `tim docker dev`            | Start the stack built from local source under `repos/` |

sources.role: how the real services behave end to end today

claims.statement: An unauthenticated user who opens the animals notification dashboard (/live-animals) is redirected to the frontend's sign-in route, which carries the requested path as a redirect parameter.
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/live-animals -> /auth/sign-in?redirect=%2Flive-animals

claims.statement: The frontend's sign-in route redirects the browser to the Defra ID authorise endpoint (the stub on localhost:3007) for the b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi policy.
claims.quote: http://localhost:3007/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi/oauth2/v2.0/authorize?serviceId=trade-imports-animals-frontend&p=b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi&response_mode=query&client_id=test-client-id&response_type=code&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A3000%2Fauth%2Fsign-in-oidc&state=[REDACTED]&scope=openid%20offline_access%20test-client-id
claims.note: The state value differs per run; redacted here as a per-session value.

claims.statement: The authorise request is an OpenID Connect authorisation-code request: response_type code, response_mode query, scope openid offline_access plus the client id, and redirect_uri pointing at the frontend's /auth/sign-in-oidc callback.
claims.quote: response_mode=query&client_id=test-client-id&response_type=code&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A3000%2Fauth%2Fsign-in-oidc

claims.statement: The authorise request names the calling service with a serviceId parameter of trade-imports-animals-frontend.
claims.quote: serviceId=trade-imports-animals-frontend

claims.statement: The Defra ID stub's authorise endpoint redirects to its own sign-in page at /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp.
claims.quote: GET 302 ... /oauth2/v2.0/authorize?... -> /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp

claims.statement: Opening the notification dashboard while signed out lands the user on the sign-in page, whose main heading is 'Sign in using Government Gateway'.
claims.quote: Sign in using Government Gateway

claims.statement: The sign-in page's browser title is 'Trade Imports Defra ID stub - GOV.UK'.
claims.quote: Trade Imports Defra ID stub - GOV.UK

claims.statement: The sign-in page's service navigation names the service 'Trade Imports Defra ID stub', and that service-name section is rendered twice, one under the other.
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 header section.govuk-service-navigation (two copies)
claims.quote: Trade Imports Defra ID stub
claims.note: The duplicate service navigation section is a rendering defect in the stub, not in the animals frontend.

claims.statement: The sign-in page carries a phase banner tagged 'Basic' with no banner text.
claims.quote: Basic

claims.statement: The sign-in page asks for a Government Gateway user ID in a text input (name crn).
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 label[for=crn], input#crn
claims.quote: Government Gateway user ID

claims.statement: The user ID field has the hint 'This could be up to 12 characters.'
claims.quote: This could be up to 12 characters.
claims.note: The hint says up to 12 characters while the error message asks for a 10-digit customer reference number (CRN); recorded, not reconciled.

claims.statement: The sign-in page asks for a password in a password-type input (name password).
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 label[for=password], input#password type=password
claims.quote: Password

claims.statement: The sign-in form submits with a button labelled 'Sign in'.
claims.quote: Sign in

claims.statement: The sign-in form posts the user ID and password as form-encoded fields crn and password to the stub's /dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp.
claims.quote: <FORM method="POST" action="/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp"> ... crn=2100010101&password=[REDACTED]

claims.statement: Below the form, the sign-in page shows a link 'I have forgotten my password'; its href is '#', so it goes nowhere.
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 main p.govuk-body a.govuk-link
claims.quote: I have forgotten my password

claims.statement: The sign-in page has a Details component with the summary 'Help signing in'.
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 details.govuk-details summary
claims.quote: Help signing in

claims.statement: The 'Help signing in' details tell the user to contact the Rural Payments Agency if they have forgotten, lost or cannot get recognised their CRN.
claims.quote: Contact the Rural Payments Agency by email or phone if: you have forgotten your CRN / you have lost your CRN / your CRN is not recognised

claims.statement: The 'Help signing in' details give an email address, a telephone number and service opening times for the Rural Payments Agency.
claims.quote: Email: testing@farming.gov.uk / Telephone: 0300 000 0000 / Service opening times: 09:00 AM to 05:00 PM
claims.note: These are stub placeholder contact details.

claims.statement: The 'Help signing in' details link to GOV.UK call charges, opening in a new tab.
claims.quote: Find out about call charges (opens in new tab)

claims.statement: The 'Help signing in' details tell a user without an account to register with the Rural Payments service, linking to www.ruralpayments.service.gov.uk.
claims.quote: Register with the Rural Payments service if you do not have an account.

claims.statement: The sign-in page uses only GOV.UK Frontend components (Input, Button, Details, Service navigation, Phase banner, Error summary) plus the app-header and app-main-wrapper hooks.
claims.ref: trace be93a action call@263 class list of main and header
claims.quote: govuk-input govuk-input--width-20 ... govuk-button ... govuk-details ... govuk-main-wrapper app-main-wrapper

claims.statement: Signing in with a user ID that is not a valid customer reference number keeps the user on the sign-in page, and the stub answers the post with HTTP 400.
claims.quote: POST 400 http://localhost:3007/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp crn=invalid&password=[REDACTED]

claims.statement: After a bad user ID, the sign-in page shows an error summary titled 'There is a problem' with the message 'Enter a valid 10-digit customer reference number (CRN) and password'.
claims.quote: There is a problem ... Error: Enter a valid 10-digit customer reference number (CRN) and password

claims.statement: Signing in with a valid user ID but a wrong password also keeps the user on the sign-in page with HTTP 400.
claims.quote: POST 400 http://localhost:3007/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/oauth2/authresp crn=2100010101&password=[REDACTED]

claims.statement: After a wrong password, the sign-in page shows the same error summary and message as for a bad user ID, so the user is not told which of the two was wrong.
claims.quote: There is a problem ... Error: Enter a valid 10-digit customer reference number (CRN) and password

claims.statement: After a failed sign-in, the user ID field keeps the value entered and the password field is empty.
claims.ref: trace 8c7b9 action call@303 input#crn, input#password; trace 57464 action call@237
claims.quote: <INPUT ... id="crn" name="crn" type="text" value="invalid" ...> <INPUT ... id="password" name="password" type="password">

claims.statement: The sign-in error summary departs from the GOV.UK Error summary pattern: the message is a span inside the list rather than a list item linking to the field, and neither input is marked with a field-level error message or error class.
claims.quote: Error: Enter a valid 10-digit customer reference number (CRN) and password
claims.note: The standard component would replace this with an li containing an anchor to #crn, plus govuk-form-group--error and an inline error message on the field. This is the stub's page, not the animals frontend's.

claims.statement: A correct user ID and password make the stub redirect to its /organisations step, which immediately redirects back to the frontend's /auth/sign-in-oidc callback with an authorisation code and the original state; no organisation choice is shown.
claims.quote: POST 302 .../oauth2/authresp -> /organisations; GET 302 http://localhost:3007/organisations -> http://localhost:3000/auth/sign-in-oidc?code=[REDACTED]&state=[REDACTED]

claims.statement: The frontend's /auth/sign-in-oidc callback redirects the signed-in user to the path held in the original redirect parameter (here the dashboard /live-animals).
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/auth/sign-in-oidc?code=[REDACTED]&state=[REDACTED] -> /live-animals

claims.statement: Signing in from the dashboard lands the user on the notification dashboard at /live-animals, whose main heading is 'Import notification service'.
claims.quote: Import notification service

claims.statement: On sign-in the frontend sets a session cookie that lasts 4 hours (Max-Age 14400), HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax.
claims.quote: session=[REDACTED]; Max-Age=14400; Expires=Wed, 07 Oct 2026 21:40:15 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/

claims.statement: On sign-in the frontend also sets sid and crumb cookies, both HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, and clears the temporary bell-defra-id cookie.
claims.quote: bell-defra-id=[REDACTED]; Max-Age=0; ... crumb=[REDACTED]; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/ ... sid=[REDACTED]; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/
claims.note: None of the cookies carries the Secure flag on the local http stack.

claims.statement: The dashboard's browser title repeats the service name: 'Import notification service - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
claims.quote: Import notification service - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: Once signed in, the service navigation names the service 'Import notification service', linking to /live-animals.
claims.quote: Import notification service

claims.statement: Once signed in, the service navigation has four items in order: Dashboard, Address book, Manage account, Log out.
claims.quote: Dashboard / Address book / Manage account / Log out

claims.statement: On the dashboard the Dashboard navigation item is marked active (aria-current) and links to /live-animals.
claims.quote: Dashboard

claims.statement: The Address book navigation item links out to the separate address book service on another origin (localhost:3002/address-book).
claims.quote: Address book

claims.statement: The Manage account navigation item has href '#', so it goes nowhere yet.
claims.quote: Manage account

claims.statement: The sign-out control is a service navigation link labelled 'Log out' that points at /auth/sign-out.
claims.quote: Log out

claims.statement: The signed-in header shows no signed-in identity: no email address, name or 'signed in as' strip appears in the header or navigation.
claims.ref: trace 0b934 action call@259 header; trace 27de2 action call@262 (auth.spec.ts:57)
claims.quote: expect(getByText('test.user11@defra.gov.uk')).toHaveCount(0)
claims.note: In trace 27de2 the count-0 assertion finished (17555.6 ms) about 2 ms before the dashboard document finished loading (17557.9 ms), and its last DOM snapshot is still the stub sign-in page, so that trace alone does not prove the absence. The absence is confirmed from the dashboard header rendered in trace 0b934 call@259, which carries no user identity.

claims.statement: Clicking Log out calls /auth/sign-out, which redirects to the Defra ID end-session URL for the same policy with a post_logout_redirect_uri pointing back at the frontend's /auth/sign-out-oidc.
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/auth/sign-out -> http://localhost:3007/idphub/b2c/b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi/signout?post_logout_redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A3000%2Fauth%2Fsign-out-oidc

claims.statement: Signing out clears the frontend's sid cookie.
claims.quote: sid=[REDACTED]; Max-Age=0; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/
claims.note: Only sid is cleared in this response; the session cookie set at sign-in is not cleared here.

claims.statement: After Log out the user lands on the Defra ID stub's page with the heading 'You have signed out'.
claims.quote: You have signed out

claims.statement: The signed-out page tells the user they can return to GOV.UK (link opens in a new tab) or close the browser window.
claims.ref: trace ca937 action call@239 (stub signout page) main p.govuk-body
claims.quote: You can return to GOV.UK or close your browser window.

claims.statement: The signed-out page stays on the stub: the browser is not sent on to the frontend's /auth/sign-out-oidc, and the page offers no link back into the import notification service.
claims.ref: trace ca937 request log (last request GET /idphub/b2c/b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi/signout, status 200)
claims.quote: GET 200 http://localhost:3007/idphub/b2c/b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi/signout?post_logout_redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A3000%2Fauth%2Fsign-out-oidc

claims.statement: After signing out, reopening the notification dashboard sends the user back through sign-in to the 'Sign in using Government Gateway' page.
claims.ref: trace 03083 action call@345, call@349; request GET /live-animals (second) (auth.spec.ts:62)
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/live-animals -> /auth/sign-in?redirect=%2Flive-animals

claims.statement: Once signed in, opening the service root / redirects to the default set's dashboard, /live-animals, which shows the 'Import notification service' heading.
claims.ref: trace 71d40 action call@250, call@254; request GET / (auth.spec.ts:40)
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/ -> /live-animals
claims.note: The spec comment says no set is served at the root any more, so / is a server-wide redirect to the default set.

claims.statement: A signed-out user who opens a page further in the journey (/live-animals/notifications/<reference>/origin) is redirected to sign-in, with that full path kept in the redirect parameter.
claims.ref: trace 68f5b action call@295, call@299; request GET /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-TBYAW8/origin (auth.spec.ts:87)
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-TBYAW8/origin -> /auth/sign-in?redirect=%2Flive-animals%2Fnotifications%2FGBN-AG-26-TBYAW8%2Forigin

claims.statement: Signing in from a deep journey link returns the user to that journey page, 'Origin of the import', rather than to the dashboard.
claims.ref: trace d79c5 action call@301, call@303; request GET /auth/sign-in-oidc (second) (auth.spec.ts:92)
claims.quote: GET 302 http://localhost:3000/auth/sign-in-oidc?code=[REDACTED]&state=[REDACTED] -> /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-BAZX13/origin

claims.statement: A draft's saved answers survive signing out and back in: on returning to the origin page after a fresh sign-in, France is still selected and the region-of-origin-code answer is still No.
claims.ref: trace d79c5 action call@301 select#countryOfOrigin-select, input#regionOfOriginCodeRequirement-2
claims.quote: <OPTION value="FR" selected="">France</OPTION> ... <INPUT ... id="regionOfOriginCodeRequirement-2" name="regionOfOriginCodeRequirement" type="radio" value="no" checked="">

claims.statement: The unauthenticated deep-link tests start from no session at all: the test keeps only cookies whose names start 'liveAnimals', and the browser held none (its cookies were trade-imports-defra-id-stub-session, crumb, sid and session), so every cookie was cleared before the deep link.
claims.ref: trace 68f5b action call@289 (cookies result), call@293 (addCookies with an empty list); trace d79c5 action call@283, call@287
claims.quote: const journeyCookies = (await pages.page.context().cookies()).filter(({ name }) => name.startsWith('liveAnimals'));
claims.note: Inferred from the cookie names the trace recorded and the empty addCookies call: the journey state is held server-side against the notification reference, not in a liveAnimals cookie.

claims.statement: The animals frontend sends a Content-Security-Policy header on the dashboard document response.
claims.quote: Content-Security-Policy: base-uri 'self';connect-src 'self' wss data:;default-src 'self';font-src 'self' data:;form-action 'self' http://localhost:3002;frame-ancestors 'none';frame-src 'self' data:;img-src 'self' data:;manifest-src 'self';media-src 'self';object-src 'none';script-src 'self' 'sha256-GUQ5ad8JK5KmEWmROf3LZd9ge94daqNvd8xy9YS1iDw=';style-src 'self';worker-src 'self'

claims.statement: The CSP restricts scripts to the frontend's own origin plus one inline script allowed by its SHA-256 hash.
claims.quote: script-src 'self' 'sha256-GUQ5ad8JK5KmEWmROf3LZd9ge94daqNvd8xy9YS1iDw='

claims.statement: The CSP lets forms post to the frontend itself and to the address book service's origin (localhost:3002).
claims.quote: form-action 'self' http://localhost:3002

claims.statement: The CSP forbids framing the frontend and forbids plugins and object embeds.
claims.quote: frame-ancestors 'none'; ... object-src 'none'

claims.statement: The CSP limits styles, fonts, images, media, manifests and workers to the frontend's own origin, with data: URIs also allowed for fonts, images, frames and connections.
claims.quote: connect-src 'self' wss data:;default-src 'self';font-src 'self' data:;frame-src 'self' data:;img-src 'self' data:;manifest-src 'self';media-src 'self';style-src 'self';worker-src 'self'

claims.statement: The CSP header is also present on the frontend's redirect responses (/live-animals 302 and /auth/sign-in 302) and on the /auth/sign-in-oidc callback, not only on rendered pages.
claims.quote: Content-Security-Policy

claims.statement: The dashboard response also sends Strict-Transport-Security for one year including subdomains.
claims.quote: strict-transport-security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains

claims.statement: The dashboard response sends X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Download-Options noopen and X-XSS-Protection '1; mode=block'.
claims.quote: x-frame-options: DENY; x-content-type-options: nosniff; x-download-options: noopen; x-xss-protection: 1; mode=block

claims.statement: The dashboard response is sent with Cache-Control no-cache.
claims.quote: cache-control: no-cache

claims.statement: The corpus never submits the sign-in form with an empty user ID or an empty password, so the message for missing credentials is not recorded.
claims.ref: auth.spec.ts (only 'invalid' user id and 'invalid' password cases); traces 8c7b9, 57464

claims.statement: No trace exercises session expiry: what a user sees when the 4-hour session cookie lapses, or whether a timeout warning is shown, is not recorded.
No trace follows the post-logout callback /auth/sign-out-oidc, so what the frontend does there (clearing the remaining session cookie, where it redirects) is not recorded.
The stub's /organisations step redirects straight back without showing a page, so the corpus never shows an organisation or business choice for a user linked to more than one organisation.
The service root / is only opened while signed in; whether an unauthenticated visit to / redirects to the default set first or straight to sign-in is not recorded.
The CSP and security headers are only recorded for the animals frontend; the Defra ID stub's sign-in and signed-out pages were not checked for them by any test.
The live-animals dashboard shows a section headed 'Filter notifications' (a level 3 heading) beside the notification list.
claims.ref: trace c7374 (search-form) expect@38; t01 snapshot of /live-animals, aside.notification-list__filters
claims.quote: Filter notifications

claims.statement: The filter section is an aside landmark labelled by the 'Filter notifications' heading and sits in the left one-third column, with the results in the right two-thirds column.
claims.quote: <ASIDE class="notification-list__filters" aria-labelledby="filter-notifications-heading">

claims.statement: The search form submits with GET to /live-animals, so a search is expressed entirely in the dashboard's query string.
claims.quote: <FORM method="get" action="/live-animals" class="notification-list__search-form" data-testid="notification-search-form">

claims.statement: The search form has one text field labelled 'Keyword or reference', named referenceNumber, empty when no search is active.
claims.ref: trace c7374 expect@40; trace b4432 snapshot call@470, #referenceNumber
claims.quote: Keyword or reference
claims.note: Rendered as <INPUT class="govuk-input" id="referenceNumber" name="referenceNumber" type="text" value="">. The label uses govuk-label--s. No hint, no character limit and no autocomplete attribute are rendered.

claims.statement: The search field has no hint text explaining what can be searched for or in what format a reference should be entered.
claims.quote:
<LABEL class="govuk-label govuk-label--s" for="referenceNumber">
    Keyword or reference
  </LABEL>
  <INPUT class="govuk-input" id="referenceNumber" name="referenceNumber" type="text" value=""></INPUT>
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of any .govuk-hint in the form group in every dashboard snapshot of the part.

claims.statement: The search form's submit button reads 'Search' and is a standard (primary) GOV.UK button.
claims.ref: trace c7374 expect@41; trace b4432 snapshot call@470
claims.quote:
<BUTTON type="submit" class="govuk-button" data-module="govuk-button" data-govuk-button-init="">
  Search
</BUTTON>

claims.statement: The search form carries the current sort as a hidden field, so a search keeps whatever sort is in force (arrivalDate,desc when none has been chosen).
claims.ref: trace b4432 snapshot call@470 and call@490, input[type=hidden][name=sort]; trace c23e0 snapshot call@615
claims.quote: <INPUT type="hidden" name="sort" value="arrivalDate,desc"></INPUT>
claims.note: After a sort to createdAt,desc the search form's hidden sort reads value="createdAt,desc" (c23e0 call@615).

claims.statement: Submitting a search loads the dashboard at /live-animals?sort=<current sort>&referenceNumber=<entered text>.
claims.ref: trace b4432 network/snapshot call@490; trace 12d83 snapshot call@501
claims.quote: http://localhost:3000/live-animals?sort=arrivalDate%2Cdesc&referenceNumber=GBN-AG-26-ZZZZZZ

claims.statement: After a search, the search field is pre-filled with the text that was searched for.
claims.quote: <INPUT class="govuk-input" id="referenceNumber" name="referenceNumber" type="text" value="GBN-AG-26-RSJ36G"></INPUT>

claims.statement: Searching by a submitted notification's complete reference number returns exactly that one notification as the only card.
claims.quote: Fill "GBN-AG-26-RSJ36G" ... Expect "toHaveCount" locator('.govuk-summary-card') expected 1

claims.statement: When a search returns one notification the results label reads 'Showing 1 Result'.
claims.quote: Showing 1 Result

claims.statement: Without a search the results label reads 'Showing 1 to 25 of N Results', giving the range shown and the total.
claims.quote: Showing 1 to 25 of 54 Results
claims.note: The total varied between traces (52 to 59) as the shared stack accumulated notifications.

claims.statement: When a search matches nothing the results label reads 'No notifications found' and no notification cards are shown.
claims.ref: trace b4432 (no-matches) expect@42, expect@43; snapshot call@490
claims.quote: No notifications found

claims.statement: A well-formed reference that matches no notification (GBN-AG-26-ZZZZZZ) gives the no-results state, not an error.
claims.quote: Fill "GBN-AG-26-ZZZZZZ"

claims.statement: Free text that is not a reference ('not-a-valid-reference') is accepted without validation: the URL carries it, no cards show, the label reads 'No notifications found' and no error summary appears.
claims.quote: Expect "not toBeVisible" locator('.govuk-error-summary')

claims.statement: The field is labelled 'Keyword or reference' but free text matched nothing, so it is unclear whether any keyword search exists beyond matching a reference number.
claims.ref: trace 0b7b1 snapshot call@451; trace c7374 expect@40
claims.quote: Keyword or reference
claims.note: An ambiguity recorded, not settled: the only free-text value tried ('not-a-valid-reference') matches no notification's data either way, so the trace cannot tell 'keyword search unsupported' from 'no keyword match'.

claims.statement: No trace searches with a partial reference, a lower-case reference or surrounding spaces, so whether matching is exact, partial or case-insensitive is not shown.
No trace submits an empty search, so what a blank search does (clears the filter, or sends referenceNumber= empty) is not shown.
In a search result, the card's View link is named 'View notification <reference>' and opens /live-animals/notifications/<reference>/notification-view.

sources.role: policy for both the live animals and the germinal products sets: which data a notification captures, each field's format and example, whether it is mandatory to proceed or optional, at which level it applies, and which commodity codes each conditional rule covers. It outranks the prototype on data and on which commodities a rule applies to, including where a prototype claim of kind 'data' says otherwise - the prototype's app/data files are demo fixtures, this page is the specification. The prototype still decides how pages look and read. A row of the Out of Scope Data Elements table de-scopes its field, which outranks any source that still describes it.

claims.statement: Level 1 is the Notification: one movement event, holding reason for import, transport, parties, Place of Destination, Border Control Post and gross weight - the things that are true of the whole consignment.

claims.quote: Level 1: Notification — one movement event. Reason for import, transport, parties, Place of Destination, Border Control Post, gross weight. Things that are true of the whole consignment.

claims.statement: Level 2 is the Commodity line, 1..N per notification: a commodity code plus its taxonomy chain (Type, Class, Species) plus a quantity - the things that are true of a specific commodity.
claims.ref: § Live Animal Data Elements, level paragraph (local-id c06b0b9ddeca), line 2
claims.quote: Level 2: Commodity line — 1..N per notification. A commodity code plus its taxonomy chain (Type, Class, Species) plus a quantity. Things that are true of a specific commodity.

claims.statement: Level 3 is the Unit record, 0..N per commodity line: identifiers for an individual animal or germinal product such as ear tag, passport, donor name/ID and collection date - the things that are true per unit.
claims.ref: § Live Animal Data Elements, level paragraph (local-id c06b0b9ddeca), line 3
claims.quote: Level 3: Unit record — 0..N per line. Identifiers for an individual animal or germinal product — ear tag, passport, donor name/ID, collection date. Things that are true per unit.

claims.statement: The page marks the accompanying document fields two different ways and does not reconcile them: the Documents intro says the attachment, reference and date of issue are 'mandatory to proceed' once a document type is selected, while the Mandatory column of all four document rows — the type row included — says 'All-or-nothing'. The page does not say which marking governs, nor whether the type field is itself part of the all-or-nothing set its selection triggers.
claims.ref: §Documents, intro paragraph (local-id 2c5298fa90db) against the Mandatory column of all 4 rows of the Documents table (ac:local-id 7a84a5d6-1cef-4985-960d-04d69086822e)
claims.quote: once a document type is selected, the attachment, reference and date of issue are   mandatory to proceed
claims.note: Both markings are named terms from the page's own Mandatory-column note in part 1 (Optional, Mandatory to proceed, Mandatory to submit, All-or-nothing, Conditional), so the two cannot be read as the same thing. The extract claims each side separately (p4-066 for the intro, p4-073/082/091/099 for the column) but never the conflict between them; a frontend has to choose one behaviour.

claims.statement: One commodity code covers several species entries in the identifier commodity lists, so the code alone does not say which identifier a line needs: 0101 appears five times in the passport list (Donkey and asses, Horse, Ponies, Zebras, Mules/hinnies or other hybrids) but once in the Horse Name list (Horse only), and 01061900 appears three times (Cats, Dogs, Ferrets) in both the passport and the tattoo lists. The page does not say how a user's commodity selection is narrowed to one of those entries.
claims.ref: §Animal Identifiers table (ac:local-id 31b8faeb-3e91-4363-8dab-381ed2141851): expands "Passport identifier commodities (6)" (2dc8b34bebe1), "Tattoo identifier commodities (2)" (3a6dbfe79b72) and "Horse Name" (c99b0c28a0d6)
claims.quote:
0101 - Donkey and asses
0101 - Horse
0101 - Ponies
0101 - Zebras
0101 - Mules, hinnies or other hybrids
claims.note: The extract makes exactly this claim for the germinal lists (p5-071, on the shared code 5119985) but nothing in the extract records it for the animal identifier lists, where it decides whether a passport, a tattoo or a horse name is asked for. The two existing cross-list claims in this range (p4-105, p4-106) compare labels between lists; this one is about one code standing for several entries within a list.

claims.statement: No accompanying document field is conditional on the commodity: unlike every Animal Identifiers row, none of the four Documents rows carries a 'Shown when the selected commodity requires ...' condition or an 'Applicable to' expand, and the page does not say whether any document type is required for particular commodities, species or reasons for import.
claims.ref: §Documents table (ac:local-id 7a84a5d6-1cef-4985-960d-04d69086822e), Conditions / Values and 'Applies at:' columns of all 4 field rows, against the Conditions / Values column of the Animal Identifiers table

The extract's p4-103 records the missing cardinality and p4-085 the missing file field, but nothing records the missing commodity conditionality — which matters because the prototype would otherwise have to guess whether, say, a CITES certificate is demanded for CITES species.

claims.statement: The Address Block marks eight of its ten fields Mandatory and only two Optional (Address Line 2 and County), so as the table is written an address record needs a name or organisation name, a transporter authorisation number, address line 1, a town or city, a postal or zip code, a country, a telephone number and an email address.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that GDS components are the toolbox, and where one is not available another tested, accessible government library (such as Ministry of Justice or Scottish Government) is used.
claims.quote: We really try to strictly head here to GDS components as a toolbox, and where that's not available, use other government libraries like a Ministry of Justice or a Scottish Government component that has been tested and meets accessibility requirements.

claims.statement: Sam rules there is a graceful degradation requirement: CSS and JavaScript may enhance behaviour, but every page must work without JavaScript, so the prototype's way of doing things may not be possible or wanted in the real service.
claims.quote: We've got a graceful degradation requirement on this, like any other GDS project, which means you can use things like CSS and JavaScript to enhance behaviour, but you need graceful degradation. It needs to be able to work without JavaScript, and that means that the way things are done in the prototype may not be possible or even desired in the real thing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that, as a pre-step for these increments, three questions are answered: is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other complementary off-the-shelf components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required. At that point it goes back to design to push back.
claims.quote: Almost as a pre-step for some of these increments, we need to get answers to that stuff: - Is it possible using off-the-shelf GDS? - If it isn't, is it using available, off-the-shelf, other complementary components? - If it isn't, why is this atypical thing strongly required? At that point, we go back to design and say, 'Come on, we don't need this.'

claims.statement: The commodity vocabulary holds values only, never the words a page shows for them: every label and hint is a copy leaf in the feature that renders it.

claims.statement: Nothing in this slice names an owner outside the service for the commodity vocabulary: the commodity types, the nine categories, the fifteen genus entries, the per-line field list and the origin country lists are all hard-coded in the set, with no call to reference-data or any other source of master data.
claims.note: Looked in services/commodities/index.js, its test, the commodity-type controller's imports and the copy bundles. The file's own docstring explains why the values live there rather than in a copy module or an obligation, but names no upstream owner. The programme's goal puts every piece of data with V4 or with MDM through reference-data, so the owner of each list is an open question this extract cannot settle.

claims.statement: The declaration is the only answer the declaration page collects.

A confirmed declaration on a draft records a late-or-on-time notification indicator worked out from the day of submission, the commodity type and the arrival date, and that indicator is system-owned rather than asked for.
A late-or-on-time indicator posted in the form is ignored: the stored indicator is the one the service works out.
The late-or-on-time indicator is written before the notification is finalised, so the submitted record already carries it.
Confirming the declaration on an amendment leaves the indicator recorded at first submission untouched, so a notification submitted on time stays on time however late the amendment is made.
A confirmed declaration that the service accepts submits the notification and opens its confirmation page.

A declaration confirmed on a notification whose answers are still incomplete is refused: nothing is submitted, the notifier is sent back to the notification view and the service logs the refusal once at info as 'Declaration refused' with the reason 'review-outstanding', the journey id and the concurrency token.

claims.statement: A submission the service rejects is refused with the reason 'submission-rejected', logged the same way, and the notifier is returned to the notification view.
A recoverable backend failure while submitting shows the declaration page again at 500 with the recoverable-failure banner and the notifier's tick still in place, rather than losing the answer.
A persistence failure that is not recoverable is not dressed up as a banner: it escapes the declaration page.
Opening or posting the declaration page for a notification that is already submitted sends the notifier to its confirmation page instead, and changes nothing about the stored notification.
A declaration posted against a notification that changed since the page was shown is sent back to the declaration page with a staleAction marker rather than overwriting the change.
claims.note: The declaration builds its routes with kit.pageRoutes, which wraps every POST in the stale-token redirect. The delete and cancel-amend pages in this slice build their routes by hand and so do not get it.

claims.statement: Every request to the set is checked by the journey entry guard before the page runs, and a request that fails it is redirected away rather than served.
The set refuses to start if any of its configuration seams is unfilled or any of its journey cookies is unregistered, so a misconfigured journey fails at boot rather than serving half a journey.
claims.quote:
* Refuse to mount a set that has not configured every required seam or
 * registered every journey cookie.
claims.note: mechanism: checks the set's own registration against the seam registry and the Hapi server's cookie states at mount time; it works on configuration, not on a notification's data.

claims.statement: The set wires one thing at a time at boot: its obligation manifest, its fulfilment bindings, its journey flow (sections, task rows, row status, flow-only keys, entry guard target, section caption and layout), its check-your-answers readiness rule, its page dispatch, its record and session stores and its journey cookie.

claims.statement: The commodity lines are a group that is always in scope, and a notification holding no line satisfies it vacuously as far as the fields below it are concerned.

claims.statement: Every commodity line must carry a quantity, whichever category it is, and it is the one per-line field with no category condition.

Whether the consignment has already arrived in Great Britain is asked only of notifications for plants for planting and for wood and cut trees.

explanation:
      'arrivalStatus applies to notifications for plants for planting and for wood and cut trees'

claims.statement: The notifier says whether the consignment has arrived rather than the service working it out from the arrival date, because one branch of the rules turns on arrival in the country and the other on arrival at the destination, and a date alone cannot tell them apart.
claims.quote:
* The notifier says so rather than the service deriving it from the arrival
 * date: reg 26(2)(a) branches on arrival in the country and reg 26(2)(b) on
 * arrival at the intended destination, and a date alone cannot say which
 * branch a consignment arriving today is in.

claims.statement: When a change of commodity type takes the arrival status out of scope, the answer already given is removed rather than kept.
claims.quote:
* A top-level scalar gate on a top-level scalar answer, so the whole
 * notification is either asked the question or not — the engine purges the
 * answer when a change of commodity type takes it out of scope.

claims.statement: Every notification must give an arrival date, whatever its commodity type, and the three different ways the question is worded are a matter for the arrival-details page, not for the rule.
claims.quote:
* One obligation for every commodity type, because every notification owes a
 * date: reg 24A(2)(a) asks potatoes for the expected date, and reg 26(2)(a)
 * asks plants and wood for the expected date of landing or, once the
 * consignment is here, the date it first arrived. Which of those three
 * sentences a notifier is shown is the arrival-details page's business — the
 * matter owed is the same one.
claims.note: Id 63e22d64-b9a0-40b4-aec6-0f5f48bdd556, status mandatory, no applyTo. Collected by the arrival-details page.

claims.statement: An expected time of arrival is asked only of potato notifications, and the answer is removed if the notification changes to another commodity type.
claims.quote:
* Reg 24A(2)(a) asks potatoes for 'the expected time and date of their

 * a potato matter and the engine purges it when a notification changes to

claims.statement: A proposed place of landing is asked only of potato notifications; plants and wood are never asked for one.

claims.statement: The shared macro kit is the save controls and the section caption; there is no macro library beyond those two, and the rest of the shared kit is view-model building and route wiring rather than markup.
claims.quote: import { dashboardPath, hubPath, pagePath, pageRoutePath } from './paths.js'
claims.note: The part's covers expects "every macro in kit.js". kit.js is a JavaScript module and defines no Nunjucks macro: it exports route options and route pairs, the chrome builders base/serverWideBase/chromeFor, the status strip, the error summary and field error view models, the save-and-continue target, the refusal and recoverable-save logging and the Ministry of Justice date field. The only Nunjucks macros in src/server/app/shared/ are saveActions (save-actions.njk) and sectionCaption (section-caption.njk), and the two partials error.njk and error-summary.njk; all are claimed above.

claims.note: The five useCase strings are quoted verbatim from the fixture: "Ware potatoes from Spain, notified before arrival", "Ware potatoes from Portugal, notified after arrival", "Seed potatoes from the Netherlands", "Spruce (Picea) from Germany, with species and EPPO code", "Conifer wood without bark from Italy, with phytosanitary treatments". claims.statement: On the commodities list, the arrival details, the identification numbers and the consignment contact pages, Back opens the page the trader pressed Save and continue on, and this is proven for a ware-potato walk and a wood walk.

On a ware-potato notification, Back goes from the commodities list to commodity-type, from the arrival details to origin, from the identification numbers to the place of destination picker, and from the consignment contact to the identification numbers.

On a wood-without-bark notification, Back goes from the arrival details to the arrival status question and from the identification numbers to the consignor picker, where a potato notification goes to origin and to the place of destination picker, so Back follows the branch the commodity type opened.
The page Back opens carries the trail without the place the trader came from, so the trail shortens by one as Back is followed.
