Country of origin stays one field over the animals country list (which already holds every country the law names), and the law's own scope lists are enforced when the notifier presses Continue: ware potatoes must come from Poland, Portugal, Romania or Spain, conifer wood without bark from Italy, France, Portugal or Spain, and other plants and wood from an EU member state

claims.statement: Docket D5-reference-status-and-lifecycle (7 rulings) keeps the reference number, status and submission model exactly as animals built them — the frontend prints whatever the backend mints, the status is the four-value lifecycle with lateness as a separate Late tag and banner, and confirmation appears only once the backend has stored the submitted record — parks the plants type-code prefix at the end of the backlog, builds post-submission Amend, Cancel amendment and Delete as in animals with Copy as new parked, and fixes the late flag at first submission.
claims.quote: The reference number, status and submission model stay exactly as animals built them: the frontend prints whatever the backend mints, the status is the four-value lifecycle with lateness shown as a separate Late tag and banner, and the confirmation page only appears once the backend has stored the submitted record with its own timestamp.

claims.statement: Docket D6-chrome-and-journey-shape (7 rulings) keeps the animals chrome exactly as it is (service name Import notification service, Alpha banner with its feedback address, two placeholder links), has the confirmation page name the relevant plant health authority with no invented helpdesk, makes the dashboard a plants-only list of this session's notifications with no cross-journey filter, gives the journey the full animals shape with the commodity entry sub-page corrected out of the run steps, keeps guidance on GOV.UK, and makes commodity-list and timing-window volatility a standing build constraint.
claims.quote: The plants journey keeps the animals chrome exactly as it is (service name Import notification service, Alpha banner and its feedback address, the two placeholder links) and the confirmation page tells the trader to contact the relevant plant health authority — APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government — with no invented helpdesk

claims.statement: Docket D7-non-functional (10 rulings) splits the ten Annex 6 non-functional and management-information items five adopted (page-level accessibility, GDS Design System conformance, 24x7 readiness, minimal trader effort, the coded values and timestamps feeding the eight metrics) and five parked (GDPR, sustainability, a live Welsh service, internal login, cross-organisation access parity), with two verified corrections: the axe tag list is widened so the WCAG 2.1 and 2.2 rules run, and a two-repo fix carries submittedAt onto the backend's notifications list.
claims.quote: The ten Annex 6 non-functional and management-information items split cleanly: five are adopted because the engine already delivers the journey's share ... and five are parked because the policy paper gives no answer (GDPR lawful basis and retention, the meaning of 'sustainable', a live Welsh service) or because Sam has ruled users and internal access out of this phase (internal login, cross-organisation access parity). Two verified corrections come out of the adoption: the axe tag list is widened so the WCAG 2.1 and 2.2 rules actually run, and a new two-repo fix extra carries submittedAt onto the backend's notifications list so the dashboard's Date submitted row stops rendering empty in real mode.

claims.statement: Ruling c-001 (D1, resolve, panel): 'Great Britain' wins in every notifier-facing string and the service applies no nation or territory check to the place-of-destination address, so a Scottish or Welsh destination is notified through this service; the SI's England-only drafting is recorded as a legal note that is not rendered and not built, because the policy paper, the SI's own destination clause (reg 26(2)(b) 'intended destination in Great Britain') and every tier-2 source say GB and no source asks the notifier to state the nation of arrival.
claims.quote: 'Great Britain' wins in every notifier-facing string (arrival-status heading and legend, arrivalDate labels by state, proposedPlaceOfLanding hint, confirmation body; the dashboard intro names no territory today — guidance-before-you-start) and the service applies no nation or territory check to the placeOfDestination address, so a Scottish or Welsh destination is notified through this service.

claims.statement: Ruling c-002 (D1, resolve, panel): the journey collects exactly the statutory timing matters — one arrivalDate for every commodity type, arrivalTime only for potatoes, arrivalStatus only for plants-for-planting and wood-and-cut-trees — a potato notification is always framed as pre-arrival with a past date accepted and flagged late rather than rejected, no actual-arrival date or time is added for potatoes, and the arrival-status page needs no authored gate because the derived gate hides it for potatoes.
claims.quote: Collect exactly the statutory matters: one arrivalDate for every commodity type; arrivalTime only when commodityType = potatoes; arrivalStatus only for plants-for-planting and wood-and-cut-trees. A potato notification is always framed as pre-arrival ('Expected date of arrival'), a past date is accepted and flagged late by lateNotificationIndicator, never rejected, and no actual-arrival date or time is added for potatoes; the arrival-status page needs no authored gate because the derived gate hides it for potatoes.

claims.statement: Ruling c-002 also sets the potato arrival-date hint 'For example, 27/3/2026. If the potatoes have already arrived, enter the date they arrived.' and keeps the potato label 'Expected date of arrival' even when the date entered is past, because potatoes have no arrived state.
claims.quote: input.hintByState = { potatoes: 'For example, 27/3/2026. If the potatoes have already arrived, enter the date they arrived.', not-yet-arrived: 'For example, 27/3/2026', already-arrived: 'For example, 27/3/2026' } — provisional copy, machine-draft Welsh pair required
claims.note: Copy is flagged provisional by the ruling itself.

claims.statement: Ruling c-006 (D1, resolve, panel): the importer selects arrivalStatus on its own single-question radios page (Yes first) for plants and wood only, placed before arrival-details and place-of-destination, and the service never derives it from the date; because the SI's two either/ors are different conditions, the destination page's already-arrived copy tells a notifier whose consignment has landed but not reached its destination to give the intended destination, so one binary status serves both clauses.
claims.quote: The importer selects arrivalStatus on its own single-question page (plants and wood only, radios Yes first) before arrival-details and place-of-destination; the service never derives it from the date.

claims.statement: Ruling c-006 sets the arrival-status answer labels to 'Yes, it has already arrived | No, it has not arrived yet' over values already-arrived and not-yet-arrived, and gives placeOfDestination a hint per state whose already-arrived wording is 'Give the address where the consignment is being kept. If it is still on its way to its intended destination, give that destination. A plant health inspector may carry out a spot check here.'
claims.quote: input.values = ["already-arrived", "not-yet-arrived"]; input.valueLabels = 'Yes, it has already arrived | No, it has not arrived yet'

claims.statement: Ruling c-029 (D1, resolve, panel): arrivalDate validates only as a real calendar date with no sanity window and no animals-style bounds, the single sourced bound being that an already-arrived date may not be after today in Europe/London, with data-max-date only in that state; expected dates accept any past or future date, lateness is computed and never validated, and a typo sanity window is parked rather than built.
claims.quote: arrivalDate validates as a real calendar date (dateText) with no sanity window and no animals-style bounds; the single bound is sourced — when arrivalStatus = already-arrived the date may not be after today in Europe/London (dateTextInRange, max only) because it is 'the date on which it first arrived'
claims.note: Its dissent records the GDS judge's [today - 1 year, today + 1 year] window and the policy judge's no-bound position, both lost.

claims.statement: Ruling c-029 sets the arrival-date error copy to 'Enter a real arrival date | Enter the arrival date | The date the consignment arrived cannot be in the future'.
claims.quote: errorCopy = 'Enter a real arrival date | Enter the arrival date | The date the consignment arrived cannot be in the future'

claims.statement: Ruling c-031 (D1, resolve, panel): the SI wording wins — plants and wood may be notified before arrival or no later than four days after the date of arrival and potatoes only at least two days before the expected date — and lateness is calendar-day arithmetic in Europe/London that ignores arrivalTime, so potatoes are late after arrivalDate minus 2 days and plants and wood after arrivalDate plus 4 days (notifying on those days is on time), a future date can still be late for potatoes but never for plants and wood, and the windows are shown up front as option hints on commodity-type and per state on arrival-status.
claims.quote: Lateness is calendar-day arithmetic in Europe/London and ignores arrivalTime — potatoes are late when the notification day is after arrivalDate minus 2 days, plants and wood when it is after arrivalDate plus 4 days (notifying on arrivalDate minus 2, or on arrivalDate plus 4, is on time); a future date can still be late for potatoes but never for plants and wood

claims.statement: Ruling c-031 sets the arrival-status option hints to 'You are making a post-arrival notification. It must be made no later than 4 days after the date of arrival. You will give the date it arrived and where it is now. | You are making a pre-arrival notification. You will give the expected date of landing and the intended destination.', with the day count supplied from the PLANTS_WOOD_DAYS_AFTER_ARRIVAL constant through a copy-function argument.
claims.quote: input.valueHints = 'You are making a post-arrival notification. It must be made no later than 4 days after the date of arrival. You will give the date it arrived and where it is now. | You are making a pre-arrival notification. You will give the expected date of landing and the intended destination.'

claims.statement: Ruling c-035 (D1, resolve, panel): after submission the late highlight appears in three places — a notification banner naming the rule breached on the confirmation page and on the submitted read-only check-your-answers view, and a red Late tag beside the status on the dashboard card — while before submission the draft check-your-answers page shows warning text when the entered date would make the notification late today and says it can still be submitted; it never blocks and there is no separate late page.
claims.quote: After submission the late highlight is shown in three places — a govukNotificationBanner naming the rule breached on the confirmation page and on the SUBMITTED read-only check-your-answers view, and a Late tag beside the status on the dashboard card; before submission the DRAFT check-your-answers page shows govukWarningText when the entered date would make the notification late if submitted today, computed by the same helper with the request clock, and says it can still be submitted. It never blocks and there is no separate late page.
claims.note: Its dissent records the policy judge's wish to park the pre-submission warning, lost 2-1.

claims.statement: Ruling c-035 makes lateNotificationIndicator a manifest obligation with system: true listed in SYSTEM_POPULATED, computed by one pure helper from (clock, commodityType, arrivalDate) called twice — with the request clock for the draft check-your-answers warning and with the finalise clock in the declaration POST, whose result is committed as a system value immediately before submitJourney only when the journey is DRAFT — so confirmation, the submitted view and the dashboard Late tag read the stored value and never recompute from submittedAt.
claims.quote: lateNotificationIndicator is a manifest obligation with system: true, listed in SYSTEM_POPULATED: one pure helper computes on-time | late from (clock, commodityType, arrivalDate) and is called twice — with the request clock for the DRAFT check-your-answers warning, and with the finalise clock in the declaration POST, whose result is committed as a system value in fulfilment immediately before submitJourney only when the journey is DRAFT (c-030); confirmation, the submitted check-your-answers view and the dashboard Late tag read the stored value and never recompute from submittedAt.
claims.note: This is the reconciled D5 shape; the original D1 text had the flag derived on read and unstored (see the reconciliation entry for c-035).

claims.statement: Ruling c-035 fixes the late copy: the banner reads 'Your notification was made outside the required timing' followed by the commodity rule string and 'It has still been accepted and recorded.', the draft warning reads 'If you submit this notification today it will be late. {rule} You can still submit it.', and the rule strings are copy functions taking the day count from the named constants — 'Notifications for potatoes must be made at least {POTATO_DAYS_BEFORE_ARRIVAL} days before the expected date of arrival.' and 'Notifications for plants for planting and wood must be made no later than {PLANTS_WOOD_DAYS_AFTER_ARRIVAL} days after the date of arrival.'
claims.quote: title Important, heading Your notification was made outside the required timing, body = the rule string for commodityType followed by It has still been accepted and recorded.; a govukTag Late (govuk-tag--red) beside the status tag on the dashboard card. Before submission: govukWarningText on the DRAFT CYA above the submit block when the helper is late for the request clock (live result, nothing stored) —"If you submit this notification today it will be late. {rule} You can still submit it."

claims.statement: Ruling timing-window-enforcement-and-late-highlight (D1, adopt, panel): the timing-window highlight is built in the first pass as a stored system value using the c-031 calendar-day rule, with no finalise hook, no backend field and no engine change, and the residual of projecting the flag into the backend NotificationDto for the regulator side is parked because Mapper A has no field for it.
claims.quote: Build it in the first pass as a stored system value: a pure lateness helper beside the check-answers feature computes on-time | late from (clock, commodityType, arrivalDate) using the c-031 calendar-day rule ... No finalise hook, no backend field, no engine change.

claims.statement: Ruling consignment-status-selected-or-derived (D1, adopt, panel): the user-selected arrivalStatus radios page (Yes first) is built for plants and wood and placed before arrival-details and place-of-destination, potatoes skip it by the derived gate, and the service never derives the status from the date in this run or later.
claims.quote: Build the user-selected arrivalStatus radios page (Yes first) for plants and wood, placed before arrival-details and place-of-destination; potatoes have no status and skip the page by the derived gate. The service never derives the status from the date, in this run or later.

claims.statement: Ruling england-vs-great-britain (D1, adopt, panel): the service is built with 'Great Britain' in every notifier-facing string and no nation check on the destination address, while the residual legal question — whether the draft SI is widened to GB or mirrored by Scottish and Welsh instruments, and whether a Scottish or Welsh destination ever routes elsewhere — is recorded as PARKED inside the behaviour and changes no page.
claims.quote: Build with 'Great Britain' in every notifier-facing string and no nation check on the destination address. The residual legal question — whether the draft SI is widened to GB or Scottish and Welsh instruments mirror it, and whether a Scottish or Welsh destination ever routes elsewhere — is recorded as PARKED (policy) inside this behaviour and changes no page.
claims.note: Its dissent records the GDS judge's wish to park the whole behaviour, lost 2-1 on labelling only.

claims.statement: Ruling arrival-date-window (D1, adopt, panel): arrivalDate is built as a real calendar date with no sanity window and no picker min/max except a maximum of today when the consignment has already arrived, taken from one bounds helper beside arrival-details; a past expected date for potatoes triggers no arrived question, is accepted and surfaces as late, and the typo sanity window is parked.
claims.quote: Build arrivalDate as a real calendar date with no sanity window and no picker min/max, except a maximum of today when arrivalStatus = already-arrived, from one bounds helper beside arrival-details. A past expected date for potatoes does not trigger an arrived question — potatoes have no arrived state — it is accepted, the potato hint says what to enter, and it surfaces as late; the typo sanity window is parked.

claims.statement: Ruling competent-authority-routing (D1, park, panel): there is no frontend increment — the journey already collects what routing needs (commodityType and placeOfDestination), never asks the notifier which authority applies, shows no 'sent to X' copy and keeps the confirmation's generic spot-check sentence — and routing, access parity and region derivation from the address are revisited when the plants backend has typed fields or an outbox.
claims.quote: Parked — no frontend increment. The notifier journey already collects what routing needs (commodityType and placeOfDestination), never asks the notifier which authority applies, shows no 'sent to X' copy, and keeps the confirmation's generic sentence that the relevant plant health authority (APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government) may carry out a spot check; routing, access parity and region derivation from the address are revisited when the plants backend has typed fields or an outbox.

claims.statement: Ruling c-003 (D4, resolve, panel): the Common Data contact is required and satisfied by the one same-as-animals contactAddress pick, because the picked address-book record carries name, address, telephone number and email address and the address-book API refuses a record without phone and email, so 'Name of person making entry', 'Contact number', 'Contact address' and 'Contact email' are all collected by that single answer and nothing is asked twice.
claims.quote: The Common Data contact is required and is satisfied by the one same-as-animals contactAddress pick: the picked address-book record carries name, address, telephone number and email address (the address-book API refuses a record without phone and email, and the plants client folds both into the address block), so 'Name of person making entry', 'Contact number', 'Contact address' and 'Contact email' are all collected by that single answer and nothing is asked twice.

claims.statement: Ruling c-003 keeps Consignment Number an optional free-text notifier reference on identification-numbers with the animals internalReferenceNumber input contract (maxText 58, pattern ^\w*$, trimmed), parks its definition — issuer, format, potato applicability and whether it ever becomes mandatory — as an open question, and flags its label 'Consignment number (optional)' and hint as provisional reconciler-invented copy; reading 'Name of person making entry' as the signed-in user is a sub-park decided by sam under standing ruling 2.
claims.quote: Consignment Number stays an optional free-text notifier reference on identification-numbers with the animals internalReferenceNumber input contract; its definition (issuer, format, potato applicability, whether it ever becomes mandatory) is parked as an open question, not built. ... The sub-park of 'Name of person making entry' as the signed-in user is decidedBy sam (standing ruling 2).

claims.statement: Ruling c-025 (D4, resolve, panel): the animals shape wins outright — the contactAddress pick is the whole contact section, the contactNumber and contactEmail obligations and the contact-details page are deleted, the contact task row completes on the pick alone, and the opening run ends at consignment-contact-select (runStep 9 after c-034's renumbering) before landing on the hub.
claims.quote: The animals shape wins outright. contactAddress (same-as-animals: flat radios over the organisation's address book, inline copy { addressId, name, address }) is the whole contact section, because the copied address block already carries telephoneNumber and emailAddress and the address-book API guarantees both are present. Delete the contactNumber and contactEmail obligations and the contact-details page; the contact task row completes on the pick alone and the opening run ends at consignment-contact-select (runStep 9 after c-034's renumbering) before landing on the hub.

claims.statement: Ruling c-025 adds Telephone number and Email address rows to the plants Check your answers Contact card, read from the inline copy, as a plants-only addition because the animals card shows name and address lines only, and records that whether 'Name of person making entry' should be the signed-in user is parked under standing ruling 2 as a new open-question behaviour name-of-person-making-entry.
claims.quote: The plants Check your answers Contact card adds Telephone number and Email address rows read from the inline copy so the trader can see what will be submitted — animals' card shows name and address lines only, so this is a plants-only addition grounded in annex:6/common-data/item:2,4 and NNS-UN-007.

claims.statement: Ruling c-026 (D4, resolve, panel): the SI wins on scope — the consignor is required for plants for planting and wood and cut trees only and is never asked for potatoes, whose crop is traced through producer and crop identification numbers instead — keeping the variant-of-animals address-book picker with { addressId } storage gated same-frame on commodityType with wipeOnExit, so consignor-select is skipped by the opening run and its hub row hidden for potatoes; a typed name-and-address fallback for an EU consignor not yet in the address book is parked.
claims.quote: The SI wins on scope: the consignor is required for plants for planting and for wood and cut trees only and is never asked for potatoes — the potato list traces the crop through producer and crop identification numbers instead. ... A typed name-and-address fallback for an EU consignor not yet in the address book is parked, not built: the trader adds it in the INS address book first, as animals traders do.

claims.statement: Ruling c-026 creates the parked behaviour consignor-typed-fallback and notes for its revisit that the INS address book requires a phone and email on every record that reg 26(2)(f) does not, so an EU consignor entry demands two facts the law does not.
claims.quote: Note for the revisit: the address book requires a phone and email on every record (AddressRequest.java) that reg 26(2)(f) does not, so an EU consignor entry demands two facts the law does not.

claims.statement: Ruling c-027 (D4, resolve, panel): countryOfOrigin keeps the animals id, page, widget, validation, label, hint and Welsh label and hint verbatim and changes only the error sentence to 'Select the country where the consignment originates from', dropping the copied Welsh error rather than shipping one that names an animal; because one copy string now differs the obligation is tagged variant-of-animals, its divergence being that error sentence and the per-category origin narrowing ruled at c-022, and the error sentence is flagged provisional copy.
claims.quote: Keep the animals id, page, widget, validation, label, hint and Welsh label and hint verbatim; change only the error sentence to 'Select the country where the consignment originates from' — one noun swapped in the animals sentence — and drop the copied Welsh error rather than ship one that names an animal
claims.note: Its dissent records the GDS judge's 'Select the country of origin' and the policy judge's 'Select the country the plants, wood or potatoes originate from', both lost to the engine judge's minimum one-noun swap.

claims.statement: Ruling c-028 (D4, resolve, panel): the declaration page and its machinery stay exactly as animals has them — single checkbox, confirmation sentence in both languages, error copy, date line, Continue, flow-only key and submit gate — but all five animals statements are replaced wholesale by three short plants statements, flagged provisional for policy and content-design sign-off with no Welsh invented, and the third-party and agent-authority clauses are parked with agent-acting-on-behalf under standing ruling 2 as a sub-park decided by sam.
claims.quote: Keep the declaration page and its machinery exactly as animals have them — the single checkbox, its confirmation sentence in English and Welsh, the error copy, the date line, Continue, the flow-only key and submit gate. Replace the five animals statements wholesale: none survives.
claims.note: Quote lightly re-joined across the resolution's first two sentences; the source reads 'exactly as animals has them'.

claims.statement: Ruling c-028 sets the three plants declaration statements: that the notifier is notifying the competent authority as required under the Plant Health National Notification Scheme; that the relevant plant health authority (APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government) may spot-check the consignment without prior notice at its place of destination or where it is currently held; and that failing to notify, notifying late or giving incorrect details may be treated as a non-compliance.
claims.quote: I am notifying the competent authority of this consignment as required under the Plant Health National Notification Scheme. | I understand that the relevant plant health authority (APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government) may carry out a spot check on this consignment, without prior notice, at its place of destination or where it is currently held. | I understand that failing to notify, notifying late or giving incorrect details may be treated as a non-compliance.
claims.note: Flagged provisionalCopy by the ruling; Welsh is machine-drafted at build, not invented in the spec.

claims.statement: Ruling c-004 (D2, resolve, panel): seed potatoes are potatoes — commodityType = potatoes, the per-line category offers seed-potatoes and ware-potatoes, and a seed-potato line takes the reg 24A matters and the two-day pre-arrival window — so the mural list-image's placement of seed potatoes under Plants for planting is not followed and 'Seed potatoes' is never a genus value.
claims.quote: Seed potatoes are potatoes: commodityType = potatoes, the per-line category offers seed-potatoes and ware-potatoes, and a seed-potato line takes the reg 24A matters (variety, quantity, intended use, producer and crop ids, time of arrival, place of landing) and the two-day pre-arrival window. The mural list-image's placement of seed potatoes under Plants for planting is not followed and 'Seed potatoes' is never a genus value.
claims.note: Ruling records no spec change: all three judges agree and the spec already carries it.

claims.statement: Ruling c-005 (D2, resolve, panel): the category value is conifer-wood-with-bark labelled 'Conifer wood with bark, or isolated bark of conifer', because the mural table's 'with mark' is a transcription typo carrying no meaning.
claims.quote: The SI wording wins: the category value is conifer-wood-with-bark, labelled 'Conifer wood with bark, or isolated bark of conifer'. The mural table's 'with mark' is a transcription typo and carries no meaning.
claims.note: The label stays provisional for the copy pass and needs Welsh before release.

claims.statement: Ruling c-007 (D2, resolve, panel): the four wood caveats are scope conditions rather than data elements, so they become the five wood category values with the bark, origin, height and form conditions in the value labels plus guidance copy, and the only extra wood data collected is size of tree and phytosanitary treatments gated on category; no question is asked about preservative treatment, bark condition or the 3-metre threshold, and the preservative exclusion moves to a hint on the category question for wood notifications with its cut-coniferous-trees exception.
claims.quote: The four wood caveats are scope conditions, not data elements: they become the five wood category values (with the bark, origin, height and form conditions in the value labels) and guidance copy; the only extra wood data collected is the two SI matters, size of tree and phytosanitary treatments, gated same-frame on category. No question is asked about preservative treatment, bark condition or the 3-metre threshold.
claims.note: Its dissent records the GDS judge's per-option hints on all five wood values and the policy judge's no-change position, both lost.

claims.statement: Ruling c-007 sets the wood category hint to 'Preservative-treated wood does not need to be notified, unless it is cut coniferous trees more than 3 metres high.' and removes the sentence 'Preservative-treated wood does not need to be notified.' from the phytosanitary treatments field, whose hint becomes 'Describe any phytosanitary treatment the wood has had, for example heat treatment (HT) or kiln drying (KD).'
claims.quote: "hintByCommodityType": { "wood-and-cut-trees": "Preservative-treated wood does not need to be notified, unless it is cut coniferous trees more than 3 metres high." }
claims.note: Provisional copy, English only until the copy pass. The move is justified because reg 26(1)(b)(iii) (cut coniferous trees) carries no preservative exclusion, so the old hint was wrong on a cut-trees line.

claims.statement: Ruling c-008 (D2, resolve, panel): '(for plants for planting)' qualifies species only, so genus is asked for plants-for-planting, trees-for-planting, hardwood-round-surface and hardwood-chips lines, species only for plants-for-planting and trees-for-planting, and the three conifer lines ask neither in the first pass; the literal reading that reg 26(2)(c) also wants a genus for conifer wood is recorded as a parked policy check.
claims.quote: '(for plants for planting)' qualifies species only. Genus is asked for plants-for-planting, trees-for-planting, hardwood-round-surface and hardwood-chips lines; species only for plants-for-planting and trees-for-planting; the three conifer lines (conifer-wood-with-bark, conifer-wood-without-bark, cut-coniferous-trees) ask neither in the first pass.
claims.note: Its dissent records the policy judge's required free-text conifer genus, lost because no source gives a conifer genus list.

claims.statement: Ruling c-009 (D2, resolve, panel): the hardwood genus constraint is Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus only, and Juglans and Pterocarya are not offered anywhere in the service because the SI footnotes record them as removed from scope, superseding the mural and Confluence lists that still carry them.
claims.quote: The hardwood genus constraint is Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus only. Juglans and Pterocarya are not offered anywhere in the service; the mural and Confluence lists that still carry them (and the mural spelling 'Juglens') are superseded by the SI footnotes.

claims.statement: Ruling c-012 (D2, resolve, panel): a notification carries one or many commodity lines — commodityLines is a collection with minEntries 1 and the error 'Add at least one commodity', built as a two-page batch (list page plus Commodity details entry sub-page) as a variant of animals' commodityLines without its catalogue search — all lines share the one commodityType chosen first, and a consignment mixing potatoes with plants or wood is two notifications.
claims.quote: A notification carries one or many commodity lines: commodityLines is a collection with minEntries 1 (error 'Add at least one commodity'), built as the two-page batch (list page plus Commodity details entry sub-page) as a variant of animals' commodityLines without its catalogue search. All lines share the one commodityType chosen first; a consignment mixing potatoes with plants or wood is two notifications.

claims.statement: Ruling c-013 (D2, resolve, panel): wipe wins — wipeOnExit stays true on every gated plants obligation and no answer is retained out of scope — and a change of commodityType after lines exist is handled in the commodity-type page's POST, which warns before the change, commits the type, drops the lines whose category is not in the new type's set via reconcileEntriesAt and redirects to the commodities list with ?removed=<n> for a banner, while the list page suppresses its zero-lines redirect for that load and never writes on GET.
claims.quote: Wipe wins: wipeOnExit = true stays on every gated plants obligation and no answer is retained out of scope. A change of commodityType after lines exist is handled in the commodity-type page's POST, not on the list page's load: the page warns before the change when lines exist, the POST commits the type and then drops the lines whose category is not in the new type's set via reconcileEntriesAt, and redirects to the commodities list with ?removed=<n> where a notification banner names what was removed; the list page suppresses its zero-lines redirect for that load and never writes on GET.

claims.statement: Ruling c-013 sets the warning before a commodity-type change to 'Changing your answer will remove the commodities you have already added.' and the banner after it to 'We removed <n> commodities that are not <commodityType label>', both provisional copy.
claims.quote: the page renders govukWarningText above the radios (provisional copy) "Changing your answer will remove the commodities you have already added."

claims.statement: Ruling c-017 (D2, resolve, panel): the genus list for plants-for-planting and trees-for-planting lines is the fifteen entries of reg 26(1)(a) with the SI's spelling and bracketed English names, the four species-level entries are offered as they stand, 'Seed potatoes' is not a genus, hardwood lines get the same control with Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus only, and the list is set-owned reference data rather than a hard-coded enum, with the details page offering only the entries allowed for the line's category and never fifteen with twelve rejected.

claims.quote: Adopt as met by the rules the spec now carries: required-ness per the SI mandate; membership for every coded value including the per-category origin narrowing and its Check-your-answers re-check; a real calendar date for arrivalDate; a new HH:MM factory for arrivalTime; a whole number of 1 or more for quantity; the animals pattern for consignmentNumber; animals' max lengths for all other text; HTTP 400 with a GOV.UK error summary on every failure.

claims.statement: Ruling live-access-synchronous-submission (D5, adopt, panel): synchronous submission is adopted as a constraint the first pass already meets — the declaration POST commits the flow-only answer, submitJourney awaits the records finalise and the confirmation page renders only once the record is submitted with its server-side timestamp — a finalise that throws re-renders the declaration with the recoverable-error message and never an optimistic confirmation, a not-ready submit returns to Check your answers, and no queue, batch or optimistic confirmation may be introduced between the notifier's submit and the persisted record.
claims.quote: Adopt as a constraint the first pass already meets, not a feature: submission is synchronous — the declaration POST commits the flow-only answer, submitJourney awaits records.finalise (real adapter POST /notifications/{journeyId}/submit; stub finalise), and the confirmation page renders only once the record is SUBMITTED with dateOfNotification stamped server-side at that moment. ... No queue, batch or optimistic confirmation may be introduced between the notifier's submit and the persisted record.
claims.note: Inspector-side live access to the record is parked with the outbox behaviour.

claims.quote: Adopted as a standing build constraint on every increment: (1) every commodity-type, category, genus and origin list is data behind the set-owned commodities service, never an obligation or copy literal; (2) the two statutory timing windows are single named constants — POTATO_DAYS_BEFORE_ARRIVAL = 2 (reg 24A(1)) and PLANTS_WOOD_DAYS_AFTER_ARRIVAL = 4 (reg 26(1)) — exported from one module beside the arrival-details feature and read by the lateness derivation and by any hint that names a window, so no other copy of the number exists; (3) the England / Great Britain wording and the authority names are copy leaves.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say what the transporter record's full field list is: it names an approval number, a private-or-commercial type and an approval status, and reuses Standard Address Block validation only "where the fields are genuinely the same", without saying which address block fields a transporter keeps or drops.

The ruling does not say where the eight hardcoded shipped transporter records live while they are parked - whether they stay in the animals frontend's services/transporters/records.js or move to the address book under decision 1 - only that they stay exactly as they are and move to inc-265.

The ruling does not say whether the forced XI country is enforced by the address book service as well as by the add form: it names the add form's hidden field and refusal of a tampered value, and the constants held in the service, without saying which service validates a commercial transporter's country on write.

The ruling does not say what a notification's picker uses to offer transporters at the transporter step: it says AddressRole exists to say which records a picker may offer for a slot and that a transporter has no role, and it backs the Transporter tab with the transporters route, without saying whether the transporter step's picker reads that route or how it filters.

sources.role: the decision on what the address book stores for an address's type and uses (EUDPA-711): "use" is renamed "role" everywhere, in the record, the API, the code, the copy keys, the tests and the spec, and an address holds the roles it can play on a notification, being place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and branch address. The address book stores roles only and requires at least one; it does not store an address type and ignores one a client sends, the address type being the INS front door's grouping of roles worked out from them. The grouping of roles into sending, receiving and branch is the address book's internal rule rather than part of its API, and it refuses roles from more than one group, and a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom. The list takes role, repeatable and any-of, and searchRole, in place of addressType, use and searchUse. A role a new notification type needs is added in code, each role in exactly one group. Addresses saved before the change are not migrated: after release the addresses collection is dropped in dev and test with CDP tooling and the address book restarted, and locally the stack is restarted. The address book's list and every address picker keep pagination even though the Design Release 2.1 prototype has none, the list API paging with page and pageSize of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, because organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses; no requirement to list an organisation's addresses unpaginated is built, which ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 later reads the other way for req-611 and so outranks on that point alone.

EUDPA-827 is the fix and has landed on the animals frontend's main. It settles conflict c-292 by keeping the plants contact picker's pagination and inset, and the contact picker pages at eight rather than five, confirmed by Ian the same day, so every picker in both journeys pages at the figure the INS address book list already uses and ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 1 set for the other pickers.
